result: They obtain optimal expected-cost benchmarks, expose up to twofold asymptotic inefficiency in a fixed pilot, and show a charged precision-aware pilot with checkpoint certification restores optimal cost for certain precision scales.
conclusion: The work provides certified sequential sampling guarantees within a specified independent-reference Bernoulli-product model, with reproducible auditors and finite-confidence overhead analysis.

title: A Graph-Theoretic Approach To Matrix Am-gm: Counterexamples And Sharp Exponential Bounds
authors: Zehua Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a graph-theoretic approach to the expected-norm matrix arithmetic--geometric mean inequality. By encoding matrix interactions with a path-supported Gram matrix, we obtain a projection family whose product is nonzero exactly when the transition graph of its index sequence is a path. This gives an intuitive explanation for failure: repeated indices can create cycles or branches that annihilate products, an effect absent for positive scalars. We prove the universal lower bound [MATH] for the ratio of the with-replacement to the without-replacement mean and show that it is asymptotically sharp on the exponential scale when [MATH]. Specifically, our construction gives a ratio [MATH], matching the lower bound's leading exponential rate over unrestricted dimensions. We also determine an explicit overlap threshold, derive exact six-factor counterexamples, and show that exponential failure can coexist with vanishing pairwise commutators.
tldr: The paper develops a graph-theoretic framework to study the failure of the expected-norm matrix arithmetic–geometric mean inequality, constructing counterexamples and proving sharp exponential bounds on the with-replacement/without-replacement ratio.
motivation: The matrix AM–GM inequality can fail when indices are repeated, unlike the scalar case, and the authors seek an intuitive structural (graph-theoretic) explanation for this failure along with quantitative bounds.
method: Matrix interactions are encoded via a path-supported Gram matrix, yielding a projection family whose product is nonzero exactly when the index-sequence transition graph is a path; this is used to construct counterexamples and prove lower bounds.
result: A universal lower bound on the ratio of with-replacement to without-replacement means is proven and shown to be asymptotically sharp on the exponential scale for unrestricted dimension, with explicit overlap thresholds and exact six-factor counterexamples.
conclusion: Exponential failure of matrix AM–GM can occur even with vanishing pairwise commutators, and the graph-theoretic projection construction provides a sharp characterization of this phenomenon.

title: Global Surveillance Under The Lens: Reconstructing Passive Dolev-Yao Intruders
authors: Paolo Modesti
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global surveillance systems record large volumes of network traffic for retrospective analysis, but packet captures alone reveal little about protocol-level semantics. This paper presents an automated, specification-guided methodology for reconstructing passive Dolev-Yao intruder executions from captured network traffic and validating the reconstructed executions against a formal protocol specification. The framework takes a PCAP capture, an AnBx specification, and the associated deployment metadata; it extracts Java-serialised objects from TCP streams, reconstructs protocol sessions and channel-to-step assignments, and generates a passive intruder that evaluates the Dolev-Yao derived checks produced by the AnBx compiler. Three reconstruction challenges are addressed: multiple serialised objects and object references within a TCP stream, ambiguity in mapping interleaved connections to concurrent protocol sessions, and semantic validation of candidate reconstructions. We evaluate the methodology on 121 protocols from the AnBx test suite. For single-session captures, the standard JDK cryptographic provider recovers 97.8% of expected objects and achieves 94.2% successful reconstruction, where success requires complete object recovery and a clean passive-intruder execution. For the 112 parallel-capable protocols, the toolchain achieves 89.3% successful reconstruction for both two and three concurrent sessions, while recovering approximately 97.2% of expected objects. Experiments with mismatched protocol-role mappings and deliberately mutated traces show that the generated Dolev-Yao checks respond to semantic inconsistencies. By making the reconstruction step explicit, the solution produces protocol-level observations on which assessments of protocol resilience and the design of defensive countermeasures can be built.
tldr: The paper presents an automated, specification-guided toolchain that reconstructs passive Dolev-Yao intruder executions from captured PCAP network traffic and validates them against AnBx protocol specifications.
motivation: Global surveillance systems collect massive packet captures, but raw traffic lacks protocol-level semantics, making it hard to assess whether observed sessions violate protocol security assumptions.
method: The framework extracts Java-serialised objects from TCP streams, reconstructs protocol sessions and channel-to-step assignments, resolves ambiguities from interleaved connections, and generates a passive Dolev-Yao intruder evaluating compiler-derived checks, validated on 121 AnBx test-suite protocols.
result: For single-session captures the JDK provider recovers 97.8% of objects with 94.2% successful reconstruction, and for 112 parallel-capable protocols reconstruction reaches 89.3% for two and three concurrent sessions while recovering ~97.2% of objects; mutated traces trigger expected Dolev-Yao check failures.
conclusion: Making the reconstruction step explicit yields protocol-level observations usable for resilience assessment and defensive countermeasure design, though the work remains in classical symbolic protocol security.

title: Breaking $\mathsf{TraintoDefend}$ Via Adaptive Neuron Clustering In Cryptanalytic Model Extraction
authors: Haojie Wu, Haolin Liu, Tianshuo Cong, Guoyan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryptanalytic model extraction poses a fundamental threat to deep learning model confidentiality by enabling precise parameter recovery with theoretical guarantees of functional equivalence. To counter this growing threat, [MATH] (NeurIPS 2025) was proposed as the first dedicated defense against cryptanalytic extraction and remains the only defense believed to be effective to date. It encourages neurons to learn similar weights so that they switch activation states together, making their individual contributions harder to distinguish. However, we notice that neurons with similar weights need not switch activation states together under small perturbations. Instead, weight similarity can cause the original clustering rule to merge signatures from distinct neurons when only a subset of their normalized weight coordinates agree. Motivated by this observation, we introduce [MATH], an adaptive clustering rule that breaks the weight-similarity defense of [MATH]. [MATH] estimates a relative scale from all jointly observed weight coordinates and uses the same scale to test both weight direction and bias consistency. Across six protected fully connected networks trained on MNIST, [MATH] raises target layer signature recovery from [MATH] to [MATH], with a maximum relative recovery error of [MATH]. Our work challenges the use of neuron weight similarity as a sufficient basis for protection and establishes adaptive evaluation as essential to assessing cryptanalytic extraction defenses.
tldr: The paper introduces an adaptive neuron-clustering attack that defeats TraintoDefend, the leading defense against cryptanalytic model extraction from deep neural networks.
motivation: Cryptanalytic extraction lets adversaries recover network parameters with functional-equivalence guarantees, and TraintoDefend was believed to be the only effective countermeasure by forcing neurons to share similar weights.
method: The authors observe that weight similarity does not imply joint activation switching under small perturbations, and propose an adaptive clustering rule that estimates a relative scale from jointly observed weight coordinates to test both weight direction and bias consistency.
result: Across six protected fully connected networks trained on MNIST, the attack raises target-layer signature recovery substantially, with a maximum relative recovery error reported for the recovered signatures.
conclusion: Neuron weight similarity is not a sufficient basis for protection, and adaptive evaluation is necessary when assessing defenses against cryptanalytic extraction.

title: Multiplicative And Additive Extractors For Low Entropy Samplable Sources Under Reduced Assumptions
authors: Marshall Ball, Eshan Chattopadhyay, Mohit Gurumukhani, Ronen Shaltiel, Yunya Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trevisan and Vadhan [TV, FOCS'00] constructed (seedless) extractors for distributions samplable by poly-size circuits that have very high min-entropy, under the very strong complexity theoretic hardness assumption that [MATH] requires size [MATH] circuits that have oracle access to [MATH]. In this paper we give three new explicit constructions of extractors for samplable distributions. First, we construct an extractor that extracts one bit, with constant error, for min-entropy [MATH], which matches the non-constructive probabilistic argument. This result uses hardness for nondeterministic circuits, and achieves the same parameters as the recent extractor of Oh and Shaltiel [OS, STOC'26] under an incomparable hardness assumption. In contrast to the extractor of [OS26], our extractor (and, similarly, the constructions below) also works for the more general class of distributions samplable with postselection (a model introduced by [BGDM, FOCS'23] that generalizes samplable and recognizable sources). Second, we construct an extractor that extracts almost all the entropy, with polynomially small error, for min-entropy [MATH], where [MATH] is an arbitrary constant. This result also uses hardness for nondeterministic circuits, and significantly improves upon the recent extractor of [Shaltiel, FOCS'25] which required a much stronger assumption. This extractor is also : a stronger notion suggested in [AASY, Comp. Complexity'16; Shaltiel, CCC'25] to make extractors for samplable distributions suitable for selecting keys for cryptographic protocols. Third, we construct an extractor that extracts almost all the entropy, with polynomially small error, for min-entropy [MATH]. This result uses hardness for circuits that have oracle access to [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs classical randomness extractors for low-entropy samplable sources under weakened complexity-theoretic hardness assumptions.
motivation: Extractors for samplable distributions are important in derandomization and cryptography, but prior constructions relied on very strong hardness assumptions or achieved weaker parameters.
method: The authors give three explicit extractor constructions using hardness assumptions for nondeterministic circuits and circuits with oracle access, extending results to distributions samplable with postselection.
result: They obtain a one-bit constant-error extractor for min-entropy matching non-constructive bounds, an almost-all-entropy extractor with polynomially small error for arbitrary constant min-entropy, and another high-output extractor under an incomparable hardness assumption.
conclusion: The work improves the assumptions and generality of extractors for samplable sources, with relevance to classical pseudorandomness and cryptographic key derivation rather than quantum information.

title: Operational Indirect Rate-Distortion Functions For Classification Tasks
authors: Yann Miguet, Elsa Dupraz, Philippe Mary
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In goal-oriented communications, indirect source coding involves two sources: a semantic source [MATH] and an observation [MATH], which is the only source available at the encoder. In this paper, we consider this framework for classification, where the decoder only needs to reconstruct [MATH]. We argue that the gap between the indirect rate-distortion function and the performance of practical learned coding schemes, such as variational information bottleneck (VIB) and variational autoencoder (VAE) architectures, comes from three effects: the latent representation, the choice of the deep neural network (DNN) architecture and training loss, and whether the encoder is aware of the task. To quantify these effects, we introduce four operational rate-distortion functions that account for the DNN architecture and the training loss, and we establish a hierarchy among them. We then derive these functions for a Gaussian mixture source, where [MATH] is the mixture state. Numerical results, both for the Gaussian mixture and for practical coding schemes on the CIFAR-100 dataset, quantify the rate loss incurred by each effect.
tldr: The paper introduces operational indirect rate-distortion functions for classification tasks in goal-oriented communications and quantifies rate losses from DNN architecture, latent representation, and task-aware encoding.
motivation: Indirect source coding with a semantic source and observation is relevant to goal-oriented communication, but practical learned coding schemes fall short of the information-theoretic indirect rate-distortion limit.
method: The authors define four operational rate-distortion functions accounting for DNN architecture and training loss, establish a hierarchy among them, and derive them for a Gaussian mixture source; they also compare with VIB/VAE-style schemes and CIFAR-100 experiments.
result: Numerical results quantify the rate loss incurred by each effect for the Gaussian mixture and for practical learned coding schemes on CIFAR-100.
conclusion: The work provides an operational rate-distortion framework that helps explain and quantify performance gaps between learned classification-oriented codes and indirect rate-distortion bounds.

title: A Little Derandomization Goes A Long Way: Unconditional Circuit Lower Bounds Using Low-Degree Pit
authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Karthik Gajulapalli, Alexander Golovnev, Ivan Mihajlin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove unconditionally that either NE contains a language requiring Boolean circuits of size at least [MATH], or [MATH], a constant-free version of Valiant's conjecture over the integers. The Boolean alternative implies that [MATH] for every constant [MATH]. Our proof gives a fine-grained variant of the connection between Polynomial Identity Testing (PIT) and circuit lower bounds established by Kabanets and Impagliazzo (2004). We show that the specific identity tests required by this argument can be performed over the integers without a derandomization assumption. Over a fixed finite field [MATH], we first give a deterministic [MATH]-time algorithm for PIT on size-[MATH] circuits computing degree-[MATH] polynomials in [MATH] variables. We further show that, for any fixed [MATH] and [MATH], improving this running time by a factor of [MATH], even nondeterministically, implies either the same Boolean lower bound or an arithmetic circuit lower bound of [MATH] for a polynomial family from [MATH]. If nondeterministic PIT instead runs in time [MATH] for infinitely many degrees [MATH], then the arithmetic lower bound strengthens to [MATH]. Over the integers, we give a deterministic PIT algorithm for syntactically set-multilinear circuits running in time [MATH], which yields the unconditional result above. Combining the Kabanets-Impagliazzo argument with range avoidance, we show that an NP algorithm for PIT over [MATH] gives a purely arithmetic win-win: either [MATH], or constant-degree polynomials of maximum circuit complexity can be constructed in FNP.
tldr: The paper proves unconditional circuit lower bounds by refining the Kabanets-Impagliazzo connection between polynomial identity testing and Boolean/arithmetic circuit lower bounds, using deterministic PIT algorithms over finite fields and the integers.
motivation: The work aims to remove derandomization assumptions from known links between PIT and circuit lower bounds, thereby obtaining unconditional lower bounds via a fine-grained derandomization approach.
method: It gives deterministic PIT algorithms for bounded-size circuits over fixed finite fields and over the integers for syntactically set-multilinear circuits, then combines a fine-grained Kabanets-Impagliazzo argument with range avoidance.
result: Unconditionally, either NE requires Boolean circuits of size at least a superpolynomial bound, or a constant-free Valiant conjecture over the integers holds; improved PIT running times yield stronger Boolean or arithmetic lower bounds.
conclusion: The paper establishes new unconditional circuit lower bounds and arithmetic win-win results, but it is a computational complexity theory contribution with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Degree Profiles Of Uniform Polynomial Consequences: Linear Lower Bounds For Nullstellensatz And Polynomial Calculus
authors: S{\o}ren Riis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proves asymptotically optimal linear degree lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus, yielding a four-way polynomial-versus-exponential proof-size classification for uniform polynomial consequences over fields of positive characteristic. The size bounds use full, explicit coefficient lists, including zeros. Apart from a fixed finite initial range, exactly one of four cases occurs: [MATH], bounded degree; [MATH], degree at least linear in the universe size [MATH]; [MATH], constant degree on some residue classes and at least linear degree on the others; or [MATH], infinitely many recurring finite degrees, with bounded-degree subsequences and finite [MATH] peaks at arbitrarily large sizes. Thus the size patterns are polynomial bounds, exponential lower bounds, a periodic mixture, or polynomial subsequences with finite exponential peaks, respectively. Underivable targets have degree [MATH], and both proof systems assign the same type. The result strengthens my 2008--2009 refutation classification and extends it to uniform consequences. The proof uses degree-preserving lifting with onset and period bounds linear in the degree. A common [MATH]-adic hardness spectrum describes the four types topologically. Distinguishing any two types is undecidable already for refutations. The linear degree bounds, four-way classification and pairwise undecidability results have been formalised and verified in Lean. The Lean formalisation, verification records and an accompanying tutorial are available in the supporting materials ([URL].
tldr: The paper establishes asymptotically optimal linear degree lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus refutations and uniform polynomial consequences over positive-characteristic fields, giving a four-way polynomial-versus-exponential proof-size classification.
motivation: Prior refutation classifications (Riis 2008-2009) left open the question of whether uniform polynomial consequences admit the same degree/size dichotomy, and whether sharp linear degree bounds could be proven.
method: The proof uses degree-preserving lifting with onset and period bounds linear in the degree, together with a common p-adic hardness spectrum that topologically distinguishes the four classification types; results are formalised and verified in Lean.
result: Exactly one of four cases occurs for sizes (polynomial bounds, exponential lower bounds, a periodic constant/linear-degree mixture, or polynomial subsequences with finite exponential peaks), with matching type assignment across both proof systems and pairwise undecidability of type distinction already for refutations.
conclusion: The work strengthens and extends the earlier refutation classification to uniform consequences, providing a topological p-adic characterization and machine-checked proofs of the linear degree bounds and undecidability results.

title: Electrical Conductivity Of A Two-dimensional Two-component Medium: Discretization And Effective Medium Approximation
authors: Yuri Yu. Tarasevich
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effective conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium is studied within a discretization scheme and the effective-medium approximation (EMA). A square lattice is superimposed on a random isotropic medium; each cell is assigned the conductivity of its majority component, and the cell is replaced by a star of four resistors. Neighboring cells are connected by an equivalent resistor whose conductivity is [MATH], [MATH], or the harmonic mean [MATH], with probabilities [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], respectively. Applying Foster's theorem and the EMA yields a closed equation for the dimensionless effective conductivity [MATH] and, after transformation, a cubic equation whose coefficients depend on [MATH] and the conductivity ratio [MATH]. The EMA predictions are compared with direct calculations on a [MATH] resistor network with periodic lateral boundary conditions and Dirichlet conditions on the top and bottom. For uncorrelated disorder, good agreement is found. For correlated disorder, when resistor conductivities are assigned according to the discretization rule from the colors of adjacent nodes, significant deviations appear and the percolation-like inflection point shifts to the right of [MATH]. The results question the validity of the correlated-disorder EMA approach and help explain discrepancies previously reported for random nanowire networks.
tldr: A classical percolation/effective-medium study of the effective conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component random resistor medium, comparing EMA predictions with direct lattice network calculations for uncorrelated and correlated disorder.
motivation: The authors aim to test whether standard correlated-disorder effective-medium approximations remain valid when conductivities are assigned by a discretization rule from a random two-component medium, motivated by discrepancies reported for random nanowire networks.
method: A square lattice is superimposed on the random medium, each cell is replaced by a star of four resistors, and neighbouring cells are connected by resistors whose conductance is the arithmetic mean, harmonic mean, or one component's value with prescribed probabilities; Foster's theorem plus EMA give a closed cubic equation for the dimensionless effective conductivity, which is compared with direct numerical solution of a finite resistor network with periodic and Dirichlet boundary conditions.
result: For uncorrelated disorder the EMA agrees well with the direct network calculations, while for correlated disorder assigned via the discretization rule significant deviations appear and the percolation-like inflection point shifts to the right of the expected value.
conclusion: The findings question the validity of the correlated-disorder EMA approach and help explain previously reported discrepancies for random nanowire networks.

title: Evolutionary Dynamics Of Collective-risk Social Dilemma Game With Risk Uncertainty And Adaptive Strategy
authors: Chuanzhi Zhou, Ju Han, Xiaojie Chen, Attila Szolnoki
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The collective-risk dilemma game constitutes the leading metaphor for studying the evolution of cooperation in populations of selfish individuals. Although most theoretical studies often consider the risk level as a fixed parameter, this may not fully reflect the uncertain nature of risk detected in real-world scenarios. Motivated by the observation that individuals can infer their game environment and accordingly adjust their actual behavior, here we investigate this game with uncertain risk. In particular, we introduce a type of adaptive agents who incur an observation cost to infer the risk level during game interactions, and subsequently decide whether to cooperate or defect based on their tolerance thresholds. We first calculate the fixation probabilities of three different strategies in a mutation-free regime. Our results show that adaptive agents are favored by natural selection at low observation costs and moderate tolerance thresholds. Moreover, the fixation of adaptive agents results in higher levels of cooperation when both parameters are relatively low. We then consider behavioral mutation and systematically explore how average cooperation level and group achievement vary with observation costs, tolerance thresholds, and mutation rates. Importantly, the main results remain intact when the mutation is considered. Furthermore, when the tolerance threshold is small, the presence of adaptive agents results in a higher cooperation level and group achievement compared to the traditional setup when only unconditional cooperators and defectors are present. This advantage, however, gradually erodes with an increasing tolerance threshold and these two quantities fall below the levels observed in the classic two-strategy case.
tldr: This paper studies evolutionary dynamics in a collective-risk social dilemma with uncertain risk and adaptive agents who pay observation costs to infer risk and adjust cooperation.
motivation: The authors argue that fixed-risk models may not capture real-world uncertainty, and that individuals may infer their environment and adapt behavior accordingly.
method: They introduce adaptive agents with observation costs and tolerance thresholds, compute fixation probabilities in a mutation-free regime, and then analyze behavioral mutation via systematic exploration of cooperation and group achievement.
result: Adaptive agents are favored at low observation costs and moderate tolerance thresholds, and their fixation can increase cooperation when both parameters are relatively low; main results persist under mutation.
conclusion: Adaptive risk inference can promote cooperation under certain conditions, but the advantage erodes as tolerance thresholds increase, falling below the classic two-strategy case.

title: Practical Semialgebraic Optimization Via Sparse Sample-Based Sum-of-Squares Programming
authors: David M. Rosen Jason Nezvadovitz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As the importance of semialgebraic optimization grows in engineering, so does the need for scalable sum-of-squares (SOS) methods. Their convex relaxations can guide mixed-integer search and often deliver certified global optima outright. Scaling traditional SOS typically requires hand-crafted bases and redundant constraints, whereas sample-based SOS numerically exploits feasible set geometry to reduce bases and build smaller, often tighter relaxations from black-box evaluations. However, discrete variables can require exponentially many samples, and each sampled equation couples all cliques, destroying correlative sparsity. In this work, we avoid enumeration and slack variables by sampling a tractable variety that contains the feasible set, with multipliers only for the omitted constraints. To recover sparsity, we introduce "separator" polynomials that split the sampled equations into local systems coupled only on clique overlaps. This yields a novel, convergent hierarchy of semidefinite programs (SDPs) with block sizes and sample requirements governed by local interactions rather than total problem size. Lastly, we show how to verify sample sufficiency and prune redundant equations numerically before solving. In robust estimation and motion planning, we obtain certifiably small optimality gaps at scales far beyond those reported for traditional sparse SOS. For example, we solve a truncated least-squares 3D registration problem with 1600 candidate correspondences in under 49 seconds using an off-the-shelf SDP solver on a laptop CPU.
tldr: The paper introduces a sparse sample-based sum-of-squares hierarchy for scalable semialgebraic optimization using separator polynomials and semidefinite programming.
motivation: Traditional sum-of-squares methods struggle to scale due to hand-crafted bases and dense constraints, while existing sample-based approaches suffer from exponential sample requirements and loss of sparsity when discrete variables are present.
method: The authors sample a tractable variety containing the feasible set, introduce separator polynomials to recover correlative sparsity, and derive a convergent hierarchy of sparse SDPs with local block sizes and sample requirements.
result: The approach achieves certifiably small optimality gaps on robust estimation and motion planning problems, including solving a 3D registration problem with 1600 correspondences in under 49 seconds on a laptop CPU.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable SOS optimization framework that exploits sparsity and numerical sampling, enabling certified global optimization at scales beyond traditional sparse SOS methods.

title: Compressions Of Linear Relations In Krein Spaces
authors: Aad Dijksma Branko \'curgus
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an orthogonal decomposition \(} = [\dotplus]}\) of a Krein space, we study compressions \({_{\mathfrak H}}(R)\) of linear relations \(R\) in \(}\) to \(\). We formulate a sufficient condition that ensures that compression commutes with taking adjoints, that is, the adjoint identity \({_{\mathfrak H}}(R^{}) = {_{\mathfrak H}}(R)^{*}\) holds. We derive preservation and reflection results for the compression of maximal dissipative, maximal symmetric, and self-adjoint linear relations. For nonnegative linear relations, the adjoint identity also implies that compression commutes with taking the Friedrichs extension. For \(\ne\{0\}\), we characterize finite dimensionality of the exit space \(}\) by universal compression properties. Finally, we give a criterion for the adjoint identity to hold in terms of bounded linear functionals on \(R\).
tldr: A pure operator-theory study of compressions of linear relations in Krein spaces, including adjoint-commutation criteria and preservation of dissipative, symmetric, and self-adjoint classes.
motivation: Compressions of operators and relations to subspaces are fundamental tools in functional analysis and extension theory, but their behaviour in indefinite-metric (Krein) spaces is not well understood.
method: Given an orthogonal decomposition of a Krein space, the authors formulate a sufficient condition for compression to commute with taking adjoints, and derive preservation/reflection results for maximal dissipative, maximal symmetric, and self-adjoint relations, plus characterizations via bounded linear functionals.
result: The adjoint identity is shown to imply commutation of compression with the Friedrichs extension for nonnegative relations, and universal compression properties are used to characterise finite dimensionality of the exit space.
conclusion: The paper provides a systematic functional-analytic framework for compressions of linear relations in Krein spaces, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Holomorphic Calculus On $L^p(\ell^q)$ I: Optimal Angles
authors: Dangyang He
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] generate a symmetric contraction semigroup. We prove a holomorphic H\"ormander calculus on [MATH] at the optimal angle [MATH], with boundary Sobolev order [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves a holomorphic Hörmander functional calculus on L^p(ell^q) for generators of symmetric contraction semigroups at an optimal angle.
motivation: The work aims to extend holomorphic functional calculus to vector-valued L^p spaces for semigroup generators with sharp angle and boundary Sobolev order.
method: It develops holomorphic Hörmander calculus on L^p(ell^q) using symmetric contraction semigroup theory and optimal-angle estimates.
result: The main result establishes the calculus at the optimal angle with a specified boundary Sobolev order.
conclusion: This is a pure functional/harmonic analysis contribution with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pit And Reconstruction For Sums Of Powers
authors: Nimrod Kaplan, Amir Shpilka, Yann Tal
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study deterministic black-box polynomial identity testing (PIT) and reconstruction for polynomials of the form \[ f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^r \alpha_i f_i(x)^d, \] where each [MATH] belongs to some underlying polynomial class [MATH]. This representation generalizes Waring decomposition, several natural small-depth circuit models, and polynomial decompositions arising in moment-based learning problems. Our main results are three lifting theorems showing that, when the outer power is sufficiently large, PIT and reconstruction for the inner class can be lifted to sums of powers. When the power degree is small, we can perform these tasks directly in some of the cases using closure properties of the underlying models. In particular we obtain the following results: \item When the inner polynomials have bounded-individual-degrees and are sparse, we obtain deterministic reconstruction for every d: the original power-sum decomposition is recovered at high degree, while at low degree the polynomial is reconstructed nonproperly by sparse interpolation. \item For sums of powers of same-order and any-order read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs, the same proper/nonproper dichotomy gives deterministic reconstruction for every powering degree. \item Explicit quasipolynomial-size hitting sets for every powering degree for several depth-5 and depth-6 circuit families, as well for the models mentioned above. Our results for high powering degree rely on the polynomial ABC theorem, which to the best of our knowledge is the first application of this theorem in the context of PIT.
tldr: The paper gives deterministic black-box polynomial identity testing (PIT) algorithms and reconstruction procedures for polynomials expressed as sums of d-th powers of polynomials from an underlying class, via three 'lifting' theorems.
motivation: Sums-of-powers representations generalize Waring decompositions, small-depth algebraic circuits and moment-based learning models, but deterministic PIT and reconstruction were not known uniformly across powering degrees.
method: The authors prove lifting theorems transferring PIT and reconstruction from the inner polynomial class to its power sums when d is large (using the polynomial ABC theorem), and handle small d directly via closure properties and sparse interpolation.
result: They obtain deterministic reconstruction for all d in the sparse bounded-individual-degree case and for read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs (same-order and any-order), plus explicit quasipolynomial-size hitting sets for several depth-5/6 circuit families.
conclusion: The work yields a proper/nonproper dichotomy for reconstruction in power-sum models and introduces the polynomial ABC theorem as a new tool for PIT, but stays entirely within algebraic complexity theory.

title: Stealthy Malicious Interference Detection In Uav Formations: A Power-Domain Signaling Game Approach
authors: Jianle Ba, Shaolong Guo, Yuntao Wang, Xin Wu, Zhou Su, Zhendong Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable intra-swarm communication is fundamental to cooperative sensing, control, and mission execution in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms. In open low-altitude shared-spectrum environments, coexisting UAVs may cause benign interference through spectrum reuse and signal leakage, while jamming UAVs may deliberately degrade critical intra-swarm links. Since a jamming UAV can adjust its transmit power to disguise signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) degradation as link fluctuation in benign interference, stealthy jammer UAV detection remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose a novel belief-driven stealthy jammer UAV detection scheme from the perspective of Bayesian security game. To capture stealthy interference in shared-spectrum UAV swarms, the interfering UAV is modeled as a hidden benign or jamming type, whose transmit power strategy induces the SINR observed by the defender. The defender updates its posterior belief from the observed SINR and decides whether to maintain normal operation or trigger defensive power boosting. We characterize pure-strategy perfect Bayesian equilibrium (PBE) conditions under separating structures with distinguishable type and pooling structures with indistinguishable observations. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme improves the defender's expected utility compared to the conventional schemes.
tldr: The paper proposes a Bayesian signaling-game framework for detecting stealthy jamming UAVs that disguise SINR degradation as benign interference in shared-spectrum UAV swarms.
motivation: In open low-altitude spectrum environments, coexisting UAVs cause benign interference while malicious jammers can adjust transmit power to hide their attacks, so distinguishing stealthy jamming from normal link fluctuation is difficult.
method: The interferer is modeled as a hidden benign-or-jamming type whose power strategy induces the defender's observed SINR; the defender updates a Bayesian posterior belief and chooses between normal operation and defensive power boosting, with pure-strategy perfect Bayesian equilibria characterized for separating and pooling structures.
result: Numerical results show the belief-driven scheme yields higher expected defender utility than conventional detection schemes.
conclusion: Game-theoretic belief updating over power-domain observations offers an effective means of detecting stealthy jammers in UAV formations, though the work is purely classical networked-systems security.

title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications Over A Relay: Benefits And Vulnerabilities
authors: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Aylin Yener
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels. A joint end-to-end design of the source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders is developed to optimize both semantic inference accuracy and perceptual reconstruction quality for image data. Relay-assisted schemes are shown to outperform direct transmission, with gains that become more pronounced in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes across different relaying strategies. Alongside these performance benefits, however, a key security vulnerability introduced by the relay is identified, and a Byzantine attack is formulated in which the relay injects structured, learned perturbations into its transmitted signal. The attack operates on intermediate communication representations subject to channel effects, with perturbations generated through a learned mapping applied at test time. It is shown to significantly degrade semantic inference accuracy at the destination. These results reveal a clear trade-off between SemCom gains and security risks in relay-assisted systems, motivating the need for secure relay designs that account for insider threats.
tldr: A joint end-to-end design of source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoder for task-oriented semantic communication is developed, showing relay gains over direct transmission while exposing a Byzantine relay attack that degrades semantic inference.
motivation: Semantic communication aims to convey task-relevant meaning rather than bits, and relays can extend coverage, but the security implications of inserting a relay into such learned pipelines are poorly understood.
method: The authors jointly train an image semantic encoder, a relay transformation, and destination decoders to optimize classification accuracy and reconstruction quality across relaying strategies, then formulate a Byzantine attack in which the relay applies a learned perturbation to intermediate representations at test time.
result: Relay-assisted schemes outperform direct transmission, with gains growing at low SNR, but the learned Byzantine perturbation significantly degrades semantic inference accuracy at the destination, revealing a performance-security trade-off.
conclusion: Relay-assisted semantic communication offers substantial benefits but introduces insider-threat vulnerabilities, motivating secure relay designs that account for malicious intermediate nodes.

title: KeHoSu: Keyed Homoglyph Substitution For Authenticated Text Provenance Over Copy-Paste Channels
authors: Andrei Alexandru Dr\u{a}ghici, Sediola Ruko, Briland Hitaj, Dorjan Hitaj
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nowadays, large language models produce text at scale, and much of it is redistributed across platforms. A moderator who finds a suspicious comment, post or article may want to know which platform generated it and for which account. In this paper we study attribution over the channel through which such text actually travels, copy-paste, which discards document metadata but keeps Unicode code points. We present KeHoSu, which turns the confusable characters of homoglyph attacks into a keyed attribution channel: the variant chosen for each carrier letter encodes one bit of an identifier made of a platform field, a user field and a truncated authentication tag. Moreover, given that reshared text is often quoted in fragments, and the placement therefore keeps no positional state, we show that KeHoSu is invariant to sentence reordering up to a constant boundary layer and depends on a partial quotation only through the retained length. We characterize the code-point channel by its capacity, removability and detectability, and provide an achievable region that relates the three. We evaluate KeHoSu over a wide range of use cases and show that the mark survived copy-paste across 18 common platforms, attributing the majority of all excerpts to the correct account at 178 letters (about two sentences) on LLM-generated stories and 167 letters (about one sentence) on standard English prose.
tldr: KeHoSu is a keyed text-provenance scheme that encodes account/platform identifiers via homoglyph substitutions in Unicode carrier letters to enable attribution across copy-paste channels.
motivation: LLMs generate text at scale, and copy-paste redistribution strips document metadata but preserves Unicode code points, creating a need for robust attribution without relying on platform metadata.
method: The authors repurpose confusable homoglyph characters as a keyed communication channel, encoding bits of an identifier plus authentication tag; they analyze invariance under sentence reordering and partial quotation and characterize the code-point channel by capacity, removability, and detectability.
result: The mark survives copy-paste across 18 common platforms, attributing most excerpts correctly at 178 letters for LLM-generated stories and 167 letters for standard English prose.
conclusion: Homoglyph-based keyed substitution can provide practical authenticated text provenance over copy-paste channels, though it is a classical information-hiding/attribution method rather than quantum information research.

title: Charge-Reversal-Based Extraction Of Muonic Ions
authors: Song Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Negative muon capture in matter is accompanied by Auger electron emission and the formation of positively charged muonic ions. This charge reversal provides a possibility for electromagnetic extraction of the products of muon capture. Here we propose a charge-reversal-based extraction scheme for muonic ions, in which negative muons are moderated and confined in a dilute gas environment before conversion, and the resulting muonic ions are subsequently accelerated and extracted by electrostatic fields. The feasibility of the concept is investigated through order-of-magnitude estimates of the competing processes, including muon moderation, muonic-ion formation, charge exchange, and acceleration in the gas medium. A magnetic-electrostatic deceleration scheme is proposed to reduce the transverse phase space of practical low-energy muon beams while retaining controlled longitudinal motion, and is directly matched to the electrostatic capture region. The analysis indicates that muonic-ion formation and extraction within the muon lifetime are not excluded by fundamental timescale constraints, although the quantitative efficiency remains uncertain because several relevant low-energy cross sections and charge-state populations are poorly constrained experimentally.
tldr: Proposes a charge-reversal-based extraction scheme for muonic ions, using moderation and confinement of negative muons in a dilute gas followed by electrostatic acceleration.
motivation: Negative muon capture in matter produces positively charged muonic ions via Auger emission, enabling electromagnetic extraction of muon capture products.
method: Order-of-magnitude estimates of competing processes (muon moderation, muonic-ion formation, charge exchange, acceleration) and a magnetic-electrostatic deceleration scheme to reduce transverse phase space of low-energy muon beams.
result: The analysis indicates that muonic-ion formation and extraction within the muon lifetime are not excluded by fundamental timescale constraints, but quantitative efficiency is uncertain due to poorly constrained low-energy cross sections.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is feasible in principle, though experimental data on relevant cross sections and charge-state populations are needed to assess practical efficiency.

title: A Componentwise Spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann Closure For Finite-volume Mhd At Finite Magnetic Reynolds Number
authors: Min Ki Jung, Brian Wynne, Francisco Saenz, Yufan Xu, Yong-Su Na, Egemen Kolemen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At finite magnetic Reynolds number, the field induced by a moving conducting fluid or solid extends into open space, so a finite mesh needs an outer boundary condition that represents the decaying exterior field. Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) codes widely use pseudo-vacuum or truncation at a finite radius. Neither condition is physically correct for a vacuum exterior, but the exact alternatives are costly or limited to simple geometries. We present a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) closure on a fixed enclosing sphere and release it as part of the open-source multi-region finite-volume solver FreeMHD. The closure matches each Cartesian component of the vector potential to its decaying exterior solution, which retains all three decaying vector-Laplace families. A meshed vacuum buffer connects non-spherical conductors to the sphere. We verify the closure with manufactured modes, sphere free decay, sphere and oblate dynamos, and a freely braking rotor. Under refinement, oblate dynamo thresholds and sphere growth rates converge toward independent spectral references, and the rotor torque matches an exact transient reference. On the same sphere, pseudo-vacuum and truncation give the larger errors predicted by their exterior models.
tldr: The paper introduces a componentwise spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann boundary closure for finite-volume magnetohydrodynamics simulations at finite magnetic Reynolds number, implemented in the open-source solver FreeMHD.
motivation: At finite magnetic Reynolds number the induced magnetic field extends into open space, and existing finite-mesh outer boundary treatments such as pseudo-vacuum or finite-radius truncation are physically incorrect for a vacuum exterior, while exact alternatives are costly or restricted to simple geometries.
method: A Dirichlet-to-Neumann closure is imposed on a fixed enclosing sphere, matching each Cartesian component of the vector potential to its decaying exterior vector-Laplace solution, with a meshed vacuum buffer connecting non-spherical conductors to the sphere; it is verified via manufactured modes, free decay, dynamo benchmarks, and a braking rotor.
result: Under mesh refinement, oblate dynamo thresholds and sphere growth rates converge to independent spectral references, the rotor torque matches an exact transient reference, and pseudo-vacuum and truncation conditions produce the larger errors predicted by their exterior models.
conclusion: The DtN closure provides an accurate, general-purpose outer boundary condition for finite-volume MHD codes in complex geometries, outperforming standard pseudo-vacuum and truncation approaches.

title: Stable Dissipative Topological Solitons In Media With Even-order Dispersion
authors: Xianan Sun, Dongdong Wang, Dumitru Mihalache, David Laroze, Boris A. Malomed, Pengfei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The formation and dynamics of dissipative solitons are governed by the interplay of dispersion and nonlinearity, alongside the gain-loss balance. While it is known that dispersion orders beyond the conventional second order support stable solitons, the possibility of the creation of dissipative topological solitons in this setting was not explored. Here, we reveal a class of stable dissipative solitons enabled by the pure-high-even-order dispersion (PHEOD), with dispersion orders m=4, 6, 8, and 10. The resulting dissipative topological solitons (DTSs) and moving topological solitons (MTSs) are dark-type structures featuring a zero-amplitude point that separates two CW backgrounds with opposite signs. In particular, the PHEOD solitons feature oscillatory tails, which are not present in the conventional dark states. The linear-stability analysis confirms full robustness of the PHEOD-supported DTSs and MTSs. We also explore collision dynamics of MTSs, whose repulsive interactions are inelastic, leading either to rebound, accompanied by emission of dispersive radiation, or complete fusion. These findings establish PHEOD as a means for the generation of new species of dissipative solitons, and broaden the variety of nonlinear modes available to experimental studies in nonlinear optics.
tldr: The paper reports stable dissipative topological solitons supported by pure high even-order dispersion in nonlinear optical media.
motivation: Dissipative solitons usually rely on second-order dispersion, and it was unclear whether stable dissipative topological solitons could exist with only higher even-order dispersion.
method: The authors theoretically study nonlinear wave models with pure high even-order dispersion for orders m=4, 6, 8, and 10, using linear stability analysis and collision simulations.
result: They find stable dark-type dissipative topological solitons and moving topological solitons with oscillatory tails, and characterize their inelastic repulsive collisions as either rebound with radiation or fusion.
conclusion: Pure high even-order dispersion provides a new route to dissipative topological solitons and expands the range of nonlinear optical modes available for experiments.

title: Simulation Of Refraction Through Voxel Volumes
authors: Rainier Mobley, Jean Michel L\'etang, Max Langer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ray tracing in X-ray science has typically been limited to descriptions where refraction occurs only at interfaces, ignoring the refraction occurring due to the continuous variations in index of refraction in the bulk of a material, as are common in biological samples like bone. We propose a method to simulate X-ray images directly on voxel grids using curved rays. We first validate this method compared to a model with an analytical solution, and then investigate the effects of voxel size, interpolation choice, and illumination to grid alignment on a few simulated test objects. From these investigations, we make several recommendations to guide simulations using these techniques.
tldr: The paper proposes a ray-tracing method that simulates X-ray refraction through continuous refractive-index variations inside voxelized volumes such as bone, validating it against an analytic model and studying numerical parameters.
motivation: Conventional X-ray ray tracing only accounts for refraction at interfaces and neglects bulk refraction from continuous index variations common in biological samples, which can bias simulated images.
method: Curved-ray tracing is performed directly on voxel grids, with the approach benchmarked against a model having an analytical solution and then tested for sensitivity to voxel size, interpolation scheme, and illumination-to-grid alignment on synthetic objects.
result: The validation confirms agreement with the analytical case, and parameter sweeps show that voxel size, interpolation choice, and grid alignment measurably affect simulated refraction artifacts, leading to practical recommendations.
conclusion: Simulating bulk refraction on voxel grids is feasible and recommended parameter choices are provided, though the work is a classical X-ray imaging/simulation study with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.

title: Solvable Macroscopic Models For Populations Of Type I Excitability Neurons With Gaussian Noise
authors: Denis S. Goldobin Maria V. Ageeva
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem. On the basis of this solution, we construct analytical expressions for the firing rate and population-mean membrane potential in terms of the real and imaginary parts of a certain universal analytic function. With this function, we generalize theoretical results to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters. Implementation of theoretical results is demonstrated and examined for two problems: the interplay between chemical and electrical synapses, and the emergence of effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks. For the latter case, it is possible to cover the scenarios where the effective noise intensity depends on Lorentzian-distributed parameters, which is not feasible directly with the diffusion approximation.
tldr: This paper derives analytic solutions for the firing statistics of noisy quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons and extends them to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters.
motivation: The authors aim to provide solvable macroscopic models for type I excitability neuron populations subject to Gaussian noise, motivated by statistical physics and computational neuroscience applications.
method: They solve the first-passage-time problem for a QIF neuron with additive Gaussian noise to obtain the mean interspike interval, then use analytic functions to construct firing-rate and mean-membrane-potential expressions for heterogeneous populations.
result: The theory yields closed-form expressions in terms of a universal analytic function and is applied to study chemical/electrical synapse interactions and effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks.
conclusion: The work offers tractable macroscopic descriptions of noisy type I excitability neural populations, but it is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Maximal Absolute Monotonicity Of Balanced Rational Functions With A Single Repeated Pole
authors: Rachid Ait-Haddou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the radius of absolute monotonicity of rational approximations to the exponential of the form \[ \phi(z)={(1-z/b)^s}, \qquad b>0,\qquad \deg P\le s, \] with approximation orders two and three. For second-order approximation, we prove that the maximal radius in degree [MATH] is [MATH] and determine the unique extremizer. Hence the conjectured value [MATH] by L\'oczi and Ketcheson (LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics, 17 (2014), no.~1, 159--205) remains valid in this case. In contrast, for every integer [MATH] we construct explicitly a rational function with rational coefficients and exact radius \[ 2s+{s^2-3s+4}>2s. \] For third-order approximation, we construct, for every [MATH], an explicit rational family with exact radius \[ 2s-1>s-1+. \] These constructions disprove the conjectures of L\'oczi and Ketcheson concerning rational functions with a single repeated pole.
tldr: The paper studies maximal absolute monotonicity radii of balanced rational approximations to the exponential with a single repeated pole, proving and disproving conjectures by Lóczi and Ketcheson.
motivation: Absolute monotonicity of rational approximations is relevant to numerical methods for stiff differential equations, particularly strong stability preserving schemes, and prior conjectures on optimal radii remained unresolved.
method: The author analyzes rational functions of the form phi(z)=(1-z/b)^s for second- and third-order approximation, constructs explicit rational families, and determines unique extremizers in certain degree regimes.
result: For second-order approximation, the conjectured maximal radius is proven valid with a unique extremizer; however, for every integer s the author constructs rational functions with exact radius exceeding 2s, disproving the prior conjectures. For third-order approximation, explicit rational families with exact radius 2s-1 are also constructed.
conclusion: The work resolves several conjectures on absolute monotonicity of single-repeated-pole rational approximations and provides explicit counterexamples to previously conjectured optimal bounds.

title: The Spectral Theory Of Cographs: A Survey, Organized By Graph Matrix
authors: Pallabi Manna, Santanu Mandal, Fernando C. Tura
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cographs, the [MATH]-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, [MATH]-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices. Within each section we collect what is known for general cographs, for the subclass of [MATH]-graphs, and where relevant, for threshold graphs. We highlight the results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Mohammadian et al., Jacobs et al., Ghorbani, Li et al., Niu et al., Lou et al., Wang at al., Mandal et al. Two structural facts are used throughout: every connected cograph has diameter at most [MATH], which ties all four distance-type matrices to the adjacency and Laplacian matrices, and the partition of the vertex set into twin classes is equitable for every one of the eight matrices, giving a uniform description of each spectrum (for the Laplacian this is the twin-reduction theory of Barik--Reddy, which we present in detail). Besides surveying the literature, we record several consequences, and mark them as such: an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix of a connected cograph, yielding an eigenvalue-free interval for the eccentricity spectrum of all connected cographs; the full distance Laplacian spectrum and its extremal eigenvalues; an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian valid for every connected graph of diameter at most [MATH]; an interlacing theorem tying the distance spectrum to the adjacency spectrum. A comparison table across all eight matrices and a list of open problems close the paper.
tldr: A survey of spectral graph theory for cographs, organized by the eight graph matrices (adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian, distance signless Laplacian).
motivation: Cographs and their subclasses (threshold graphs, P4-graphs) form a central testing ground for spectral graph theory, and recent years have produced many scattered results that lack a unified treatment.
method: Literature survey structured by matrix type, exploiting two structural facts: connected cographs have diameter at most 2, and twin classes give an equitable partition for all eight matrices, yielding uniform spectral descriptions (including detailed presentation of Barik–Reddy twin reduction for the Laplacian).
result: Collects known spectral results for cographs and subclasses and adds new consequences, including an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix, an eigenvalue-free interval for eccentricity spectra of all connected cographs, full distance Laplacian spectrum and extremal eigenvalues, an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian at diameter ≤ 2, and an interlacing theorem linking distance and adjacency spectra.
conclusion: The survey provides a comparative table across the eight matrices and a list of open problems, serving as a reference for spectral graph theory on cographs.

title: A Physics-based Adaptive Low-rank Method For 6d Vlasov Simulations
authors: Lukas Einkemmer Fabio Cassini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numerical simulation of kinetic plasma models in six-dimensional phase space poses significant computational and memory challenges, particularly when considering modern high-performance computing architectures. In this work, we propose an adaptive dynamical low-rank approach for the efficient solution of the 6D Vlasov--Poisson system. Our strategy is an extension of the projector-splitting dynamical low-rank integrator. The algorithm changes the rank based on physical observables (e.g., the electric field and energy) as opposed to controlling the error in the distribution function. Our approach is memory efficient in the sense that only rank [MATH] objects are required to implement the scheme. This makes the algorithm suitable for performing high-dimensional computations on graphic processing units. Comparisons with rank adaptive Basis-Update & Galerkin integrators exhibit both significant memory savings and reduction in run time. We show, by presenting a variety of 6D benchmark experiments implemented in the C++/CUDA low-rank framework Ensign, that our technique allows us to run simulations with a significantly smaller rank, while still preserving the physical fidelity. Thus, the approach substantially reduces memory footprint and computational cost and enables simulations that are prohibitively expensive for full-rank or less memory-efficient low-rank schemes.
tldr: The authors introduce an adaptive dynamical low-rank integrator for six-dimensional Vlasov–Poisson simulations whose rank is controlled by physical observables, cutting memory and runtime on GPUs.
motivation: Kinetic plasma simulations in 6D phase space are severely limited by memory and compute cost, especially on modern GPU architectures where conventional full-rank or error-controlled low-rank schemes remain prohibitively expensive.
method: They extend the projector-splitting dynamical low-rank integrator so that the rank is adapted based on physical observables such as the electric field and energy rather than on the distribution-function error, requiring only rank-sized objects and implemented in the C++/CUDA Ensign framework.
result: Benchmark 6D experiments show substantially smaller ranks, significant memory savings, and reduced run time compared with rank-adaptive Basis-Update and Galerkin integrators while preserving physical fidelity.
conclusion: Physics-driven rank adaptation makes high-dimensional Vlasov simulations feasible on GPUs and enables computations that are impractical for full-rank or less memory-efficient low-rank schemes.

title: Elapsed-Service-Time-Aware Preemption For Age Of Information Minimization
authors: Mohammad Moltafet, Nail Akar, Sennur Ulukus, Marian Codreanu, Roy D. Yates
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the age of information and peak age of information in status update systems with an arbitrary number of independent sources sharing a single server with generally distributed service times. We consider a general age-dependent self-preemptive policy in which an in-service update from source [MATH] is preempted by a new same-source arrival with a probability [MATH] that depends on the elapsed service time [MATH]. This formulation subsumes the non-preemptive, fully self-preemptive, and probabilistically preemptive policies as special cases, and also accommodates threshold-based preemption. We develop a unified analytical framework based on non-homogeneous absorbing continuous-time Markov chains and semi-Markov chains to derive explicit expressions for the average age of information and peak age of information of each source under general per-source service-time distributions and age-dependent preemption rules. The framework applies to both single-source and multi-source systems and enables joint tuning of per-source preemption parameters. Numerical results for fifteen service-time distributions in the single-source setting reveal that the benefits of preemption depend strongly on the service-time hazard-rate structure, with threshold-based preemption providing its most notable additional gains over age-independent policies for distributions with unimodal hazard rates. For a dual-source system with lognormal service times, jointly tuned threshold-based preemption achieves lower sum average age of information and peak age of information than the considered age-independent policies, highlighting the importance of cross-source interactions in preemption decisions.
tldr: The paper derives exact expressions for average and peak age of information in multi-source status-update systems under an elapsed-service-time-dependent self-preemptive policy.
motivation: Preemption decisions in status-update networks are usually age-independent; the authors argue that conditioning preemption on how long an update has already been in service can significantly improve freshness metrics.
method: A unified analytical framework based on non-homogeneous absorbing continuous-time Markov chains and semi-Markov chains is developed to compute per-source average and peak age of information for general service-time distributions and general age-dependent preemption probabilities.
result: Numerical study over fifteen service-time distributions shows preemption gains depend strongly on the hazard-rate structure, with threshold-based preemption giving the largest extra gains for unimodal hazards; in a dual-source lognormal system, jointly tuned threshold preemption beats age-independent policies.
conclusion: Elapsed-service-time-aware preemption and cross-source interaction are important design levers for minimizing age of information and peak age of information in shared-server status-update systems.

title: Multiplayer Stopping Games With A Conditionally Atomless Filtration
authors: Robert Samuel Simon, Eilon Solan, Grzegorz Tomkowicz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stopping games are the multiplayer generalization of optimal stopping problems, in which each player independently chooses when to stop, and the payoff depends on who stops first and when. While the existence of [MATH]-equilibria in two-player stopping games with integrable payoffs is known, the multiplayer case has remained open. We prove that every multiplayer stopping game in discrete time with integrable payoff process admits an [MATH]-equilibrium for every [MATH], provided the filtration is conditionally atomless. This condition is satisfied, in particular, when the underlying probability space is [MATH] endowed with the uniform measure and its natural filtration. Our method also shows that every three-player stopping game, without the restriction to conditionally atomless filtration, admits an [MATH]-equilibrium, for every [MATH]. The proof combines techniques developed for two-player stopping games and for multiplayer quitting games, with a key new insight: the richness encoded in a conditionally atomless filtration can substitute for an external public randomization device, allowing players to coordinate without an explicit coordination signal.
tldr: The paper proves existence of epsilon-equilibria in multiplayer stopping games under a conditionally atomless filtration, using the filtration to replace an external public randomization device.
motivation: Existence of equilibria in multiplayer stopping games has remained open, while the two-player case with integrable payoffs is known.
method: The proof combines techniques from two-player stopping games and multiplayer quitting games, with a key insight that conditional atomlessness of the filtration provides sufficient richness to coordinate players without an explicit public randomization signal.
result: Every multiplayer stopping game in discrete time with integrable payoff process admits an epsilon-equilibrium for every epsilon greater than zero when the filtration is conditionally atomless; additionally, every three-player stopping game admits such an equilibrium without that restriction.
conclusion: The work resolves a game-theoretic existence question and highlights a structural role of atomless filtrations in multiplayer stochastic games, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cubic Optimization Over Three Nonnegative Integers Is NP-hard
authors: Linchuan Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that deciding whether an integer cubic polynomial takes a value at most one over three nonnegative integers is NP-hard. Hardness holds even when every feasible objective value is a positive integer, so every constructed instance has a finite, attained minimum. This establishes a sharp dimension boundary for the tractability of cubic integer optimization in fixed dimension. Our reduction from positive 1-in-3 satisfiability encodes Boolean constraints as modular conditions and uses an algebraic norm to construct a cubic objective whose minimum is one exactly for satisfiable formulas. The resulting six-parameter threshold language is NP-complete and admits short exponent certificates.
tldr: The paper proves NP-hardness of deciding whether a cubic integer polynomial over three nonnegative integers can take a value at most one.
motivation: It aims to establish a sharp dimension boundary for the tractability of cubic integer optimization in fixed dimension.
method: The proof reduces from positive 1-in-3 satisfiability, encoding Boolean constraints as modular conditions and using an algebraic norm to construct a cubic objective.
result: The constructed six-parameter threshold language is NP-complete and admits short exponent certificates, with hardness holding even when every feasible objective value is a positive integer.
conclusion: Cubic optimization over three nonnegative integers is NP-hard, marking a dimension threshold for fixed-dimension cubic integer optimization.

title: Last-Iterate Convergence Of Stochastic Gradient Methods For Unbounded Problems
authors: Kevin Kurian Thomas Vaidyan, Ahmet Alacaoglu, Michael P. Friedlander
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods have attracted significant attention as practical implementations typically return the last iterate instead of an average of the iterates. In this paper, we study two approaches for analyzing the last-iterate convergence of proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods without bounded domain or bounded variance assumptions, where black-box variational inference serves as a running example. Under two related assumptions relaxing the bounded variance, we show near-optimal anytime rate [MATH] for the last iterate. Moreover, when the horizon [MATH] is known, we remove the logarithmic factor and obtain the optimal order [MATH], matching the order known under bounded variance or bounded domain assumptions.
tldr: This paper establishes last-iterate convergence rates for proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods without bounded domain or bounded variance assumptions.
motivation: Practical implementations return the last iterate rather than an averaged iterate, but most convergence theory relies on bounded domains or bounded variance, so new analyses are needed for unbounded problems such as black-box variational inference.
method: The authors analyze proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods under two relaxed assumptions that replace bounded variance, deriving anytime and horizon-dependent convergence guarantees for the last iterate.
result: They obtain a near-optimal anytime rate with a logarithmic factor and, when the horizon is known, remove that logarithmic factor to achieve the optimal order matching bounded-variance or bounded-domain results.
conclusion: Last-iterate convergence can be guaranteed at optimal rates even in unbounded settings, extending stochastic optimization theory to problems like black-box variational inference.

title: Energy-conserving Scheme For A Shallow-water Model With Capillary Effects
authors: Sudarshan Kumar K, Boniface Nkonga, Praveen Chandrashekar
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.
tldr: The paper develops a fully discrete energy-conserving numerical scheme for shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects.
motivation: Capillary effects introduce third-order differential equations, making stable and energy-conserving numerical approximations challenging for shallow-water and thin-film models.
method: The authors use an augmented second-order formulation and construct a fully discrete scheme that conserves total energy for quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models.
result: Numerical experiments show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.
conclusion: The scheme provides a robust energy-conserving approach for capillary shallow-water and thin-film flow simulations, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Random Reshuffling For Smooth Convex Optimization: Dominates Stochastic Gradient Descent
authors: Zijian Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is one of the most classical optimization algorithms with favorable theoretical guarantees, yet its practical implementation differs subtly from its well-known form and is often referred to as Shuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent (Shuffling SGD). A particularly popular strategy in Shuffling SGD is Random Reshuffling (RR), which has achieved great empirical success. Despite its strong performance, RR has long been considered a heuristic due to a lack of theoretical support. Over the last decade, people have finally established provable convergence rates for RR, thus justifying its observed superiority. However, for smooth convex optimization, two clouds over the convergence theory of RR remain. According to current theory, Shuffling SGD under RR converges only when the stepsize is smaller than a threshold proportional to [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of summands in the objective (or the number of data points). Consequently, the optimally tuned theoretical rate of Shuffling SGD under RR is strictly worse than that of SGD when the number of epochs is smaller than another threshold proportional to [MATH]. These two restrictions heavily limit the applicability of existing theories and leave a critical mismatch with practice. In this work, for the first time, we prove that RR dominates SGD in smooth convex optimization for any reasonable stepsize after any finite number of epochs, thereby addressing a longstanding open question. Moreover, we establish new algorithm-dependent lower bounds for RR and SGD, respectively. Altogether, these results yield (nearly) sharp worst-case characterizations of RR and SGD. Furthermore, we develop a shuffling-based method to optimize functions satisfying the quadratic growth condition, a strict relaxation of strong convexity, and derive a new complexity bound improving existing results proved under stronger assumptions.
tldr: The paper proves that Random Reshuffling (RR) dominates Stochastic Gradient Descent for smooth convex optimization across any reasonable stepsize and finite number of epochs, with new matching lower bounds.
motivation: RR enjoys strong empirical success but existing convergence theory only guarantees convergence for stepsizes below a threshold proportional to 1/n, making its theoretical rate worse than SGD for small epoch counts—a mismatch with practice.
method: The authors derive new convergence analyses and algorithm-dependent lower bounds for RR and SGD in the smooth convex setting, and extend the analysis to functions satisfying the quadratic growth condition via a shuffling-based method.
result: RR is shown to dominate SGD for any reasonable stepsize after any finite number of epochs, yielding nearly sharp worst-case characterizations for both algorithms, plus an improved complexity bound under quadratic growth.
conclusion: The work resolves a longstanding open question in optimization theory and provides tight, practice-aligned guarantees for random reshuffling.

title: Projection-Free Gradient Tracking Neurodynamic For Distributed Nonnegative Sparse Optimization
authors: Juntao Li, Qihang Guo, Deyuan Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a continuous-time, projection-free neurodynamic system based on gradient tracking for distributed nonnegative sparse optimization. Unlike traditional methods, our approach avoids projecting states onto the feasible set. Instead, it employs gradient tracking to estimate average gradients under heterogeneous costs, coupling primal and dual dynamics such that feasibility and sparsity emerge naturally from the equilibrium conditions. The system ensures unique solutions through a locally Lipschitz vector field and guarantees that every equilibrium corresponds to an exact KKT point.
