We establish rigorous convergence guarantees for convex objectives through three distinct analytical layers. These include a centralized kernel rate, a computable distributed rate derived from Jacobian analysis without restrictive stability assumptions, and a global exponential stability proof based on Lur'e system theory. Our analysis quantitatively separates these layers, revealing that the convergence rate is primarily limited by graph sparsity and remains robust to variations in momentum time scales. Numerical experiments on strongly convex quadratic problems validate the theoretical rates, demonstrate effective active set recovery, and show that the system maintains stable tail convergence rates even under strong local heterogeneity.
tldr: The paper proposes a continuous-time projection-free neurodynamic system with gradient tracking for distributed nonnegative sparse optimization.
motivation: Distributed optimization methods often rely on projections onto feasible sets, which can be computationally costly, and need to handle heterogeneous local objectives while recovering sparse solutions.
method: The authors design a projection-free continuous-time dynamical system that couples primal and dual dynamics, using gradient tracking to estimate average gradients and ensure feasibility and sparsity from equilibrium conditions.
result: They establish convergence guarantees for convex objectives via three analytical layers—centralized kernel rate, computable distributed rate from Jacobian analysis, and global exponential stability from Lur'e system theory—and validate the rates numerically on strongly convex quadratic problems.
conclusion: The system achieves stable tail convergence under strong heterogeneity and recovers active sets effectively, with convergence primarily limited by graph sparsity.

title: Singular Values Of Iterated Aluthge Transforms Of Compact Operators
authors: Hranislav Stankovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Yamazaki proved that the norms of the iterated Aluthge transforms of an operator converge to its spectral radius, and Ando showed that for matrices the singular values of the iterates converge to the moduli of the eigenvalues. We prove that the latter holds for every compact operator on a Hilbert space and every generalized Aluthge transform [MATH] with [MATH]: for every [MATH], the [MATH]-th singular value of the [MATH]-th iterate converges to [MATH], and the products of the [MATH] largest singular values, as well as the Ky Fan norms, decrease monotonically to their limits. This is the Aluthge counterpart of the Yamamoto--Davis theorem. We also determine the limit in the Schatten [MATH]-norm whenever [MATH] belongs to a strictly smaller Schatten class.
tldr: The paper proves convergence and monotonicity properties of singular values and Ky Fan norms under generalized iterated Aluthge transforms of compact Hilbert-space operators.
motivation: The work extends known matrix results of Ando and the Yamamoto-Davis theorem to compact operators and generalized Aluthge transforms, addressing a pure operator-theoretic convergence question.
method: It analyzes iterated generalized Aluthge transforms of compact operators and establishes convergence of individual singular values, products of largest singular values, and Ky Fan norms, including Schatten-norm limits under class assumptions.
result: For every compact operator and admissible generalized transform, the k-th singular value of the n-th iterate converges to the modulus of the corresponding eigenvalue, while products of largest singular values and Ky Fan norms decrease monotonically to their limits.
conclusion: The paper provides an Aluthge-transform counterpart of the Yamamoto-Davis theorem for compact operators, contributing to functional analysis and operator theory rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Over-the-Scene Computation: Illumination-Programmed Functional Sensing Of Unresolvable Populations
authors: Christopher G. Brinton Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decisions about dense populations depend on how much will cross a boundary by a deadline and when the first member arrives. Conventional radar forms a range-Doppler map, whose cells add noise and whose detections merge unresolved members. We introduce over-the-scene computation, where illumination makes the scene compute such functionals without resolving members. With random echo phases, a correlator's mean output energy sums member reflectivities weighted by a kernel set by the waveform and template. The waveform's ambiguity function is this computation's transfer function, determining computable functionals and their noise cost. One readout aggregates members over a small delay-Doppler area but along a line segment growing with duration, longest for the chirp of matching slope among constant-envelope waveforms. Members predicted to share a range lie on such a line, so a chirp's mean beat spectrum is the predicted range profile at a look-ahead horizon set by its rate. For unbiased estimation, a Cramer-Rao bound over all equal-energy waveforms favors resolving members above unit signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and grouping weaker ones into unit-SNR sets. At 0.65 members per cell, -10 dB member SNR, and one sweep, the chirp's bin sum inside the boundary comes within 16% of this bound in root-mean-square error and, with 77 times fewer samples per horizon, outperforms every unbiased estimator from a coherent processing interval of equal dwell, bandwidth, and energy. No finite set of waveform-template probes determines an unconstrained Rayleigh-fluctuating population's first arrival, but bisection localizes it if first arrivals outweigh later arrivals' sidelobes.
tldr: The paper introduces 'over-the-scene computation', a radar framework in which the illumination waveform itself performs functional computation on dense, unresolvable populations (e.g., counting crossings by a deadline, first arrival time) rather than forming a conventional range-Doppler map.
motivation: Conventional radar range-Doppler processing merges unresolved targets and accumulates noise per cell, making aggregate functionals over dense populations hard to estimate; the authors seek a method that computes such functionals directly without resolving individual members.
method: They analyze the correlator's mean output energy with random echo phases, treating the waveform ambiguity function as the transfer function of the computation, and derive a Cramér-Rao bound over all equal-energy waveforms to characterize unbiased estimation and noise cost.
result: For a chirp waveform at 0.65 members per cell and -10 dB member SNR with one sweep, the bin-sum estimate inside the boundary comes within 16% RMSE of the bound and beats all unbiased estimators from a coherent processing interval of equal dwell, bandwidth, and energy using 77x fewer samples.
conclusion: Waveform-programmed sensing can compute population functionals efficiently, though no finite waveform-template probe set determines first arrival for an unconstrained Rayleigh-fluctuating population; bisection localizes it when first arrivals dominate later arrivals' sidelobes.

title: The Fixed-point Proportion Of Latt\`es Maps
authors: Xin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How often does an element of the geometric iterated Galois group of a Latt\`es map fix a vertex of the tree? Let A/K be an abelian variety over a separably closed field of characteristic 0, G <= Aut(A,0) finite, and alpha an isogeny of degree at least 2 normalising G. The Latt\`es map on X=A/G has a preimage tree governed by alpha-power torsion; we determine the fixed-point proportion in every dimension. For zeta in G the weight is the reciprocal of the number of fixed points of zeta in alpha-power torsion (zero if infinite); equivalently, it is a product of p-adic absolute values of determinants on the alpha-active subspaces; for scalar alpha=m the proportion is (1/|G|) times the sum over 1 != zeta in G of the product over p dividing m of the p-adic absolute value of det(1 - zeta | H_1(A,Z)). We deduce positivity and vanishing criteria, prove the groups G_infinity are martingale groups, determine the limit law, and reduce groups with translations to the fixed-origin case. In dimension one we determine ten values for scalar multipliers and nontrivial G <= Aut(E,0), and for the eight quadratic Latt\`es classes the proportions are 1/8, 1/4 and 5/16. Bridy-Jones-Kelsey-Lodge exclude the Latt\`es case from their main theorem; their Theorem 2.5 periodic-point bound is attained, via reductions modulo split primes p = 1 (mod 4), for the map (x^2+a)/(x^2-a), a^2 = -1, and we settle the exceptional case of the Fari\~na-Asategui-Radi conjecture.
tldr: The paper determines the fixed-point proportion of geometric iterated Galois groups arising from Lattès maps on abelian varieties A/G, in every dimension.
motivation: The fixed-point proportion (the probability that a random element of the arboreal Galois group fixes a vertex) is a natural invariant of arithmetic dynamics, and the Lattès case was excluded from the main theorems of earlier work (Bridy–Jones–Kelsey–Lodge), leaving it open.
method: The author expresses the fixed-point proportion via weights given by reciprocals of fixed-point counts of zeta in alpha-power torsion, equivalently as products of p-adic absolute values of determinants on alpha-active subspaces of H_1(A,Z).
result: The proportion is computed in all dimensions (e.g., (1/|G|)·sum over nontrivial zeta of products over p|m of |det(1-zeta|H_1)|_p for scalar alpha=m), positivity/vanishing criteria are derived, the groups G_infinity are shown to be martingale groups, and in dimension one eight quadratic Lattès classes give proportions 1/8, 1/4, 5/16.
conclusion: The results attain the periodic-point bound of Bridy–Jones–Kelsey–Lodge via reductions mod split primes for (x^2+a)/(x^2-a), and settle the exceptional case of the Fariña–Asategui–Radi conjecture.

title: Polynomial-Time Computation Of Extensive-Form Proper Equilibria In Two-Player Zero-Sum Games
authors: Sam Ganzfried
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for computing an exact extensive-form proper equilibrium in a finite two-player zero-sum extensive-form game with perfect recall and rational data. Properness is understood in the agent normal form: an action at an information set is penalized relative to a better action while all other local behavioral choices, including the player's own future actions, remain fixed. Our algorithm assigns each information set a geometric permutahedron of allowable action probabilities. A scaled doubly stochastic representation embeds these restrictions in a polynomial-size sequence-form polytope; a saddle point then satisfies the local [MATH]-properness inequalities. To obtain an exact equilibrium rather than a solution at an arbitrarily small numerical perturbation, we establish sign stability of a parametric linear system, construct a persistent feasible basis, and extract the limits of behavioral ratios. The resulting probabilities are rational and have polynomial encoding length, including at information sets whose realization probabilities vanish.
tldr: The paper presents a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for computing an exact extensive-form proper equilibrium in finite two-player zero-sum games with perfect recall.
motivation: Proper equilibrium is a refinement of Nash equilibrium, but exact polynomial-time computation in extensive-form zero-sum games has remained challenging.
method: The algorithm uses geometric permutahedra and a scaled doubly stochastic representation embedded in a sequence-form polytope, then establishes sign stability and a persistent feasible basis to extract exact rational limits.
result: It computes an exact proper equilibrium in polynomial time with rational probabilities of polynomial encoding length, including at information sets with vanishing realization probabilities.
conclusion: This advances algorithmic game theory by providing an exact polynomial-time method for a foundational equilibrium refinement, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Typed Knowledge Over Constructive Institutions
authors: Hans-Martin Will
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Type theories designed for mathematics or program verification need only that a proposition holds; proof irrelevance in conversion erases, at the kernel level, how a claim was established. A persistent knowledge store, by contrast, must retain that record: who established a claim, by which derivation or external tool, and under which assumptions. This volume presents the theory of Eigenius---a store of typed knowledge over constructive institutions---and develops its metatheory from that requirement. The kernel theory is a dependent type theory with cumulative universes, an impredicative universe of propositions, inductive families, and an intensional identity type. Proof irrelevance is an axiom with an explicit witness rather than a conversion rule, so proofs of a proposition are provably equal yet remain distinct terms. Definitional equality is joinability under an orthogonal rewriting system---confluent, injective on type formers, and decidable by a type-free test---while a separate subsumption judgment covers universe cumulativity, codomain-covariant function types, and declared class inclusions. We prove consistency via a set-theoretic model; develop a justification logic over the kernel's propositions to track evidence and support; organize environments as an institution so that store extensions are signature morphisms and external verdicts enter via comorphisms; formulate a typed knowledge-graph theory with records, classes, and refinements; and prove the correctness of conversion, normalization by evaluation, and bidirectional type checking relative to termination. A Lean 4 formalization accompanies the volume.
tldr: The paper presents Eigenius, a formal theory of a persistent store of typed knowledge built on a dependent type theory with explicit proof irrelevance, justification logic, and an institutional organization of knowledge-graph records.
motivation: Mathematics-oriented type theories erase proof provenance via proof irrelevance in conversion, but a knowledge store must retain who asserted a claim, by what derivation or external tool, and under which assumptions.
method: The authors define a dependently typed kernel with cumulative universes, an impredicative proposition universe, inductive families, and intensional identity, treating proof irrelevance as an axiomatized witness; definitional equality is characterized as joinability in an orthogonal rewriting system, with consistency shown via a set-theoretic model, evidence tracked by a justification logic, environments organized as an institution with signature morphisms and comorphisms, and a typed knowledge-graph theory with records, classes, and refinements.
result: They prove consistency, correctness of conversion, normalization by evaluation, and bidirectional type checking relative to termination, and accompany the development with a Lean 4 formalization.
conclusion: Eigenius offers a principled foundation for provenance-preserving, machine-checked knowledge bases, bridging type theory, justification logic, and institutional semantics.

title: CANMentor: A Large-Small Model Collaboration Framework For Can Bus Intrusion Detection
authors: Zhiquan Liu (the College Of Cyber Security, Jinan University), Haolin Gao (the College Of Cyber Security, Jinan University), Bo Wu (the College Of Cyber Security, Jinan University), Jingjing Guo (the School Of Cyber Engineering, Xidian University), Heng Sun (the College Of Information Science And Technology, Jinan University), Jianfeng Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Controller Area Network (CAN) bus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making real-time intrusion detection necessary. However, resource and latency constraints limit vehicle-side intrusion detection systems (IDSs) to lightweight models, whose detection performance and generalization can degrade under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. Meanwhile, uploading original CAN messages to the cloud for more powerful model inference risks exposing sensitive vehicle information. We propose CANMentor, a large-small model collaboration framework in which a cloud-side large language model (LLM) teacher supervises vehicle-side lightweight IDS models for CAN bus intrusion detection. Each vehicle first performs local inference, and a privacy-aware generator then produces proxies from the original CAN messages for cloud-side teacher inference to protect data privacy. The vehicle uses the teacher prediction only when the response arrives within a prescribed latency bound and otherwise retains the local prediction; all returned teacher logits are converted into soft targets for periodic knowledge distillation. On non-IID partitions of the ROAD dataset and the HCRL Car-Hacking dataset, knowledge distillation yields maximum relative Macro F1 improvements of 25.01% and 20.79%, respectively. Teacher predictions also improve detection accuracy for CAN messages near the local decision boundary by 38.71-42.00 percentage points.
tldr: CANMentor is a cloud-vehicle collaboration framework where an LLM teacher supervises lightweight CAN bus intrusion detection models via privacy-aware proxy generation and knowledge distillation.
motivation: CAN bus lacks built-in security, but vehicle-side IDSs are constrained to lightweight models that degrade under non-IID data, while uploading raw CAN messages to the cloud risks privacy leakage.
method: The framework performs local inference on each vehicle, uses a privacy-aware generator to create proxies for cloud-side LLM teacher inference, applies teacher predictions only within a latency bound, and distills returned logits into soft targets for periodic knowledge distillation.
result: On non-IID ROAD and HCRL Car-Hacking partitions, knowledge distillation improves Macro F1 by up to 25.01% and 20.79%, respectively, and teacher predictions improve accuracy near the local decision boundary by 38.71-42.00 percentage points.
conclusion: Large-small model collaboration with privacy-preserving proxies and latency-aware teacher supervision can enhance lightweight CAN bus intrusion detection without exposing raw vehicle data.

title: Cloudy Skies: Early Detection Of Jamming Against Iridium Leo Satellite-IoT Links
authors: Ingrid Huso, Giulia Fliescher, Savio Sciancalepore, Gabriele Oligeri
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite-IoT systems increasingly provide connectivity to mobile assets in remote areas, which makes their resilience to radio-frequency jamming a growing concern. Timely jamming detection, i.e., before complete link failure, has been studied for terrestrial networks and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), but it remains unclear whether these approaches are effective on LEO links, where propagation varies rapidly, the received signal is weak, and jamming should be detected from the messages that are still correctly received. This paper investigates the extent to which jamming of Iridium LEO satellite-IoT links can be detected from the physical layer of correctly decoded messages. To this aim, we collect and publicly release a real-world dataset of Iridium messages under 47 jamming conditions, spanning two propagation environments, static and mobile receivers, and different jammer distances, powers, and signal types. We use this dataset to analyze three one-class autoencoder-based anomaly detectors operating on physical-layer information and compare them against two signal-quality estimators commonly used as jamming indicators in GNSS-based applications. Our results show that detectability is governed by the rise of the receiver noise floor, through which jammer power, distance, and receiver mobility act. With 1000-sample chunks, i.e., 40 ms of received signal at 25,000 samples per second (about four correctly decoded messages), the autoencoders reach an AUC of at least 0.84 whenever a noise jammer raises the noise floor by at least 9 dB, whereas the [MATH] and SNR estimators fail, since received messages, although correctly decoded, retain a high SNR under jamming. Therefore, timely jamming detection for LEO satellite-IoT links like Iridium should rely on physical-layer information beyond the signal-quality metrics adopted in the GNSS domain.
tldr: The paper studies early detection of radio-frequency jamming on Iridium LEO satellite-IoT links using one-class autoencoder anomaly detectors applied to physical-layer features of correctly decoded messages.
motivation: LEO satellite-IoT systems serve remote mobile assets and their resilience to jamming is a growing concern, but it is unclear whether jamming-detection methods developed for terrestrial networks and GNSS transfer to LEO links with fast-varying propagation and weak signals.
method: The authors release a real-world dataset of Iridium messages collected under 47 jamming conditions across two propagation environments, static and mobile receivers, and varying jammer distance, power, and signal type, then benchmark three one-class autoencoder detectors against two GNSS-style signal-quality estimators (SNR-based).
result: Detectability is governed by the rise of the receiver noise floor; with 1000-sample chunks (about four decoded messages) the autoencoders reach AUC of at least 0.84 when a noise jammer raises the noise floor by at least 9 dB, while SNR-style estimators fail because decoded messages retain high SNR under jamming.
conclusion: Timely jamming detection for LEO satellite-IoT links such as Iridium should rely on physical-layer information beyond the signal-quality metrics used in the GNSS domain.

title: Dispersive Corrections To Electromagnetic Energy And Power Flux Are Imprints Of Eliminated Degrees Of Freedom
authors: Constantin Simovski Stanislav Maslovski
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a spatially dispersive medium the electromagnetic energy and flux are given by the frequency and wave-vector derivatives of the constitutive parameters, a result known as the Agranovich--Ginzburg (AG) formulas. Here, we clarify the physical meaning of the derivative terms in these relations and show that they measure the energy and flux carried by the degrees of freedom of the internal field-matter dynamics that the Maxwellian constitutive description hides. We construct an extended state-space model of such dynamics for a wide class of temporally and spatially dispersive media, from which the Maxwellian constitutive relations follow upon elimination of the internal variables, the effective material operator resulting from the Schur complement of the eliminated internal block. A congruence identity relates this complement to the extended state-space description, which allows us to extend the AG formulas to general bianisotropic media and to establish the conditions of their validity in the presence of dissipation. The AG dispersive corrections are thus the imprints of the eliminated degrees of freedom rather than independent constitutive postulates. They hold for fields driven at arbitrary real frequency and wave vector, and not only for eigenmodes, provided that the sources act on the fields alone and that any dissipation is carried by the electromagnetic subsystem. We verify the construction on the Lorentz, Drude, magnetized-plasma, and hydrodynamic models, the last of which describes a nonlocal metal. Additionally, a capacitively loaded wire medium is treated in the Supplemental Material.
tldr: The paper clarifies that dispersive corrections to electromagnetic energy and power flux in material media arise from hidden internal degrees of freedom eliminated in the Maxwellian constitutive description.
motivation: The Agranovich--Ginzburg formulas are widely used for electromagnetic energy and flux in dispersive media, but the physical meaning of their derivative terms is often unclear.
method: The authors construct an extended state-space model for temporally and spatially dispersive media and use a Schur complement/congruence identity to relate eliminated internal variables to effective constitutive parameters.
result: They extend the Agranovich--Ginzburg formulas to general bianisotropic media, establish validity conditions under dissipation, and verify the construction on Lorentz, Drude, magnetized-plasma, and hydrodynamic models.
conclusion: Dispersive corrections are not independent postulates but imprints of eliminated degrees of freedom, holding for arbitrary real frequency and wave vector when sources act only on the electromagnetic subsystem.

title: Randomized Parallel Complexity Of Weakly Convex Optimization
authors: Kang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the minimum number of query rounds needed to find approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions, measured by the gradient of the Moreau envelope. Each round permits multiple simultaneous queries. In the stated parameter regime, the standard subgradient rate is optimal in sufficiently high dimensions, even for randomized algorithms making polynomially many parallel queries per round. We then show how the order structure of the real line enables faster search: a deterministic algorithm using only function values achieves logarithmic round complexity, with a further reduction through parallel queries. Matching lower bounds hold even when each query returns the entire subdifferential. Together, these results clarify the role of dimension in determining the benefits of parallel queries for weakly convex optimization.
tldr: The paper studies randomized parallel query-round complexity for finding approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions.
motivation: It aims to determine how many parallel query rounds are necessary and sufficient for weakly convex optimization, and when parallelization can outperform standard subgradient methods.
method: The analysis establishes upper and lower bounds on query rounds under parallel queries, including deterministic function-value-only algorithms exploiting the order structure of the real line.
result: In sufficiently high dimensions the standard subgradient rate is optimal even for randomized algorithms with polynomially many parallel queries per round, while function-value methods achieve logarithmic round complexity with matching lower bounds.
conclusion: The work clarifies the role of dimension in whether parallel queries provide speedups for weakly convex optimization.

title: Newton Steps Are Faster For Linear Complementarity Problems
authors: Haoyuan Ma, L\'aszl\'o A. V\'egh, Adrian Vladu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear Complementarity Problems (LCPs) with sufficient matrices form a well-studied class of problems, dating back from the foundational works of Cottle and Dantzig (1968). LCPs capture convex quadratic programs, and admit reductions from problems such as discounted stochastic games or mean-payoff games. While the original approach for solving these problems was based on pivoting methods, in their 1991 book, Kojima, Megiddo, Noma, and Yoshise introduced an interior point method (IPM) with running time that is polynomial in the input size, but which depends linearly on a certain parameter called the handicap number of the matrix. Despite the ensuing rich literature on sufficient LCP IPMs, the linear dependence on the handicap number has not been improved since then. We present an IPM whose running time depends on the square root of the handicap number. The algorithm can decrease the duality gap by a constant factor in [MATH] iterations. Curiously, this can already be achieved using standard Newton updates. We analyze the IPM in a norm defined by a local weighting, where centralizing Newton steps quadratically converge to the central path, without any dependence on the handicap number. The weights arise from a characterization by Rump (Linear Algebra and Its Applications, 1997, 1998, 2003) of the sign-real spectral radius and its relation to sufficiency; another ingredient of our proof is a new operator norm characterization of the handicap number. Moreover, the connection to Rump's work also enables us to show coNP-completeness of testing sufficiency, and approximation hardness of the handicap number.
tldr: This paper improves interior-point methods for linear complementarity problems with sufficient matrices by reducing the runtime dependence on the handicap number from linear to square-root.
motivation: LCPs with sufficient matrices generalize convex quadratic programs and capture problems such as discounted stochastic games, but existing polynomial-time interior-point methods depend linearly on the handicap number, which has not been improved since 1991.
method: The authors design and analyze an interior-point method using standard Newton updates in a locally weighted norm, leveraging Rump's characterization of the sign-real spectral radius and a new operator-norm characterization of the handicap number.
result: The algorithm decreases the duality gap by a constant factor in a number of iterations depending on the square root of the handicap number; the paper also shows coNP-completeness of testing sufficiency and approximation hardness of the handicap number.
conclusion: The work provides a faster interior-point method for sufficient LCPs and establishes complexity-theoretic hardness results related to sufficiency and the handicap number.

title: A New Characterization Of Streaming Decidability Of Boolean CSPs Under Deletions
authors: Aditya Bandekar, Amatya Sharma, Santhoshini Velusamy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the single-pass streaming space complexity of Boolean CSP satisfiability in the strict-turnstile model for every fixed constraint language [MATH] of [MATH]-ary Boolean relations that is not trivially satisfiable. Constraints can be inserted or deleted with nonnegative multiplicities; satisfiability is decided for those remaining at the end. While Sharma and Velusamy [ESA 2026] characterized insertion-only complexity via non-redundancy (up to logarithmic factors), we show that strict-turnstile complexity is governed by the integer capturing degree. For [MATH], let [MATH] be the minimum degree of an integer-coefficient polynomial vanishing exactly on [MATH] over the Boolean hypercube, and set [MATH]. On polynomial-length streams, we obtain an [MATH]-space randomized algorithm and an [MATH] lower bound for all algorithms. Moreover, our algorithm outputs a sparse instance preserving every satisfying assignment. This yields, to our knowledge, the first insertion-only versus turnstile separation for streaming CSPs. It also differs from the Fourier-degree characterization of exact optimization by Kol, Paramonov, Saxena, and Yu [ITCS 2023]. For [MATH], [MATH]-XOR with literals has three distinct space complexities: [MATH] for insertion-only satisfiability, [MATH] for strict-turnstile satisfiability, and [MATH] for exact optimization in either model.
tldr: The paper characterizes the single-pass streaming space complexity of Boolean CSP satisfiability in the strict-turnstile model via a new algebraic parameter called integer capturing degree.
motivation: Prior work characterized insertion-only streaming complexity of Boolean CSPs, but the more general strict-turnstile model with deletions remained less understood.
method: The authors define the integer capturing degree of a Boolean relation and use it to derive randomized streaming algorithms and lower bounds for satisfiability under insertions and deletions.
result: They obtain matching up to logarithmic factors upper and lower space bounds, give a sparse-instance-preserving algorithm, and establish the first insertion-only versus turnstile separation for streaming CSPs.
conclusion: Strict-turnstile streaming complexity of Boolean CSP satisfiability is governed by the integer capturing degree rather than by insertion-only non-redundancy or Fourier degree.

title: Noma Assisted Coordinated Beam Hopping For Vleo Satellite Communication Systems
authors: Jiayang Kang, Xinwei Yue, Xuyang Zhang, Tian Li, Peng Yang, Chunyu Pan, Shaoli Kang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a non-orthogonal multiple access assisted coordinated beam hopping (NOMA-CBH) scheme in multidimensional very low Earth orbit (VLEO) satellite communication systems, where multiple satellites employ CBH and coordinated beams jointly serve ground users and a dedicated ground station (GS). To characterize the VLEO-specific propagation environment, we develop a channel model that incorporates atmospheric attenuation, Doppler effects, and pointing perturbations. Building upon this architecture and channel model, a low-complexity decoupled (LCD) algorithm is designed to optimize beam scheduling and power allocation. We further derive closed-form outage probability expressions for the ground users and the GS, perform asymptotic analysis to characterize their diversity orders, and evaluate the delay-limited throughput. Simulation results demonstrate that: i) The NOMA-CBH with LCD algorithm achieves an enhanced system sum rate relative to orthogonal multiple access with coordinated beam hopping (OMA-CBH); ii) Across the considered heterogeneous traffic-demand operating points, the NOMA-CBH scheme achieves higher aggregate delivered traffic than the benchmark schemes; and iii) The outage performance of NOMA-CBH is better than that of OMA-CBH.
tldr: This paper proposes a NOMA-assisted coordinated beam hopping scheme for VLEO satellite communications and analyzes its outage and throughput performance.
motivation: The work aims to improve spectral efficiency and traffic delivery in multidimensional very low Earth orbit satellite systems under heterogeneous user demands.
method: The authors develop a VLEO channel model including atmospheric attenuation, Doppler effects, and pointing perturbations, then design a low-complexity decoupled algorithm for beam scheduling and power allocation and derive closed-form outage probability expressions.
result: Simulations show that NOMA-CBH with the proposed algorithm achieves higher sum rate and aggregate delivered traffic than OMA-CBH benchmarks, with improved outage performance.
conclusion: NOMA-CBH is presented as an effective approach for enhancing VLEO satellite communication system performance, but the work is classical wireless communications and not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unified Design Of Short Mode-evolution Couplers
authors: S. -Y. Tseng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Short mode-evolution couplers have been designed with several seemingly different approaches, including fast quasi-adiabatic dynamics (FAQUAD), counter-diabatic (CD) driving realized by tailoring waveguide widths and spacing, CD driving realized by axis bending, and numerical optimization of the coupler geometry. Using exact two-mode coupled-mode theory in the Kramers--Henneberger frame of the bent coupler, we show that these approaches belong to the same design space. The three geometric parameters, width difference, spacing, and axis tilt, act on the light through two functions only: the coupling strength, set by the spacing, and an effective detuning, set by the width difference and the axis curvature. The gauge, bent, and mixed realizations of a CD coupler are therefore the same device and have the same bandwidth. The bandwidth is set by the angle [MATH] between the light and the field that steers it on the Bloch sphere, integrated along the device as [MATH], and for a CD coupler this integral is set by the reference alone. This leads to a lithography-aware design rule: make the reference as adiabatic as the minimum gap allows, by narrowing its spacing at the anticrossing, and let exact CD suppress the remaining nonadiabatic coupling. In beam propagation method (BPM) simulations on a polymer platform, a 500\um{} coupler designed this way, without numerical optimization, maintains [MATH] transfer over 274~nm at a minimum edge gap of 1.05\um, compared with 150~nm for the CD coupler of a fixed-spacing reference at nearly the same gap. Particle swarm optimization of the geometry with BPM in the loop does not exceed the design rule. Three-dimensional BPM of the BCB channel waveguides also confirms these conclusions.
tldr: This paper unifies several design approaches for short mode-evolution couplers in integrated photonics by showing they occupy a single design space governed by coupling strength and effective detuning.
motivation: Short mode-evolution couplers have been designed via seemingly distinct methods (FAQUAD, counter-diabatic driving via width/spacing tailoring or axis bending, and numerical optimization), and the authors aim to demonstrate these are fundamentally the same device.
method: Using exact two-mode coupled-mode theory in the Kramers-Henneberger frame for bent couplers, the authors express all three geometric knobs (width difference, spacing, axis tilt) as two functions—coupling strength and effective detuning—and validate with 2D/3D beam propagation method simulations on a polymer platform.
result: A 500 um coupler designed by the proposed lithography-aware rule achieves transfer over 274 nm bandwidth at 1.05 um minimum edge gap, versus 150 nm for a fixed-spacing reference; particle swarm optimization does not outperform the design rule.
conclusion: The unified framework yields a practical, optimization-free design rule for broadband short couplers and clarifies that gauge, bent, and mixed counter-diabatic realizations are the same device with identical bandwidth.

title: Support In The Domain Of Numerical Algorithms In The Education Of Future Secondary School Mathematics Teachers
authors: Josef Dan\v{e}k
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents web-based applets designed primarily to educate future mathematics teachers in the field of numerical algorithms and, secondarily, to serve high school students themselves. The applets allow users to explore the behaviour of basic numerical algorithms as applied to fundamental mathematical topics taught at high schools. The advantage is that no software is required, and students can intuitively test how a given method works by adjusting specific problem parameters, not only by viewing a list of approximate solutions, but especially through graphical output. Furthermore, they have access to multiple different methods for comparison.
tldr: Presents web-based interactive applets for teaching numerical algorithms to future secondary-school mathematics teachers and their students.
motivation: Numerical methods are hard to grasp from static lists of approximate solutions, and teachers need accessible tools that require no installed software.
method: Browser-based applets let users adjust parameters of basic numerical algorithms on standard high-school topics and compare several methods graphically.
result: The applets provide graphical output and side-by-side method comparison, enabling intuitive exploration of algorithm behaviour without software installation.
conclusion: The tool is intended primarily for pre-service teacher education and secondarily for high-school students, with no connection to quantum information science.

title: Boundary Projection Acceleration For 2d One-cell Inversions In The Scattering Limit
authors: Joanna Piper Morgan, Todd S. Palmer, Ilham Variansyah, Kyle E. Niemeyer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient radiation transport on modern high-performance computers requires algorithms that expose spatial parallelism while maintaining robust convergence. One-cell inversion (OCI) replaces the spatially sequential transport sweep of source iteration with a cell-local solve, making discrete ordinates transport space-parallel, but its spectral radius approaches unity in diffusive problems, and existing accelerators such as transport synthetic acceleration reintroduce sweeps. Here we show that projecting the OCI residual onto a low-order angular space on cell boundaries accelerates convergence in scattering-dominated problems without a transport sweep. We implement the projection in a two-dimensional simple-corner-balance discretization with two angular bases: a linear ([MATH]) basis and one augmented with a quadrant moment ([MATH]). Fourier analysis of an infinite homogeneous medium shows that both corrections reduce the spectral radius in optically thick, highly scattering regimes, with [MATH] being most effective. Across several test problems, including a modified version of the void-duct streaming benchmark, the method accelerates diffusive and scattering cases but does not uniformly improve convergence in streaming dominated problems. We also find that [MATH] is a more robust accelerator than [MATH] in situations where the flux has strong angular variation. Boundary projection substantially improves OCI convergence in diffusive regimes, and these results delimit the regimes that require additional stabilization or richer projection spaces.
tldr: The paper introduces a boundary projection acceleration scheme for one-cell inversion (OCI) discrete ordinates radiation transport that avoids transport sweeps and improves convergence in diffusive, scattering-dominated regimes.
motivation: OCI makes radiation transport space-parallel but its spectral radius approaches unity in optically thick, highly scattering problems, and existing accelerators like transport synthetic acceleration reintroduce the sequential sweep that OCI was designed to eliminate.
method: The OCI residual is projected onto a low-order angular space on cell boundaries within a two-dimensional simple-corner-balance discretization, using two angular bases (a linear basis and one augmented with a quadrant moment), analyzed via Fourier analysis of an infinite homogeneous medium and tested on benchmark problems.
result: Both corrections reduce the spectral radius in optically thick, highly scattering media with the augmented basis most effective, accelerating diffusive and scattering cases but failing to uniformly improve streaming-dominated problems where strong angular flux variation favors the more robust basis.
conclusion: Boundary projection substantially improves OCI convergence in diffusive regimes and delimits the regimes requiring additional stabilization or richer projection spaces.

title: Classification And $C_2$-cofiniteness Of Rational Vertex Operator Algebras Generated In Low Conformal Weights
authors: Ruochen Yang Jiancai Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain classification results for rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights. More precisely, we prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of OZ type strongly generated by its conformal weight two subspace [MATH] is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of Virasoro minimal models. We also prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type generated as a vertex algebra by its conformal weight one subspace [MATH] is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of simple affine vertex operator algebras associated with finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras at positive integral levels. Consequently, Zhu's conjecture that rationality implies [MATH]-cofiniteness holds for both classes, and every such rational vertex operator algebra is regular.
tldr: This paper classifies rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights and proves Zhu's conjecture for two such classes.
motivation: Rational vertex operator algebras are central objects in conformal field theory and representation theory, and Zhu's conjecture connecting rationality to C2-cofiniteness has been an important open problem.
method: The authors use structural and representation-theoretic arguments for vertex operator algebras to classify OZ-type algebras strongly generated by weight-two states and CFT-type algebras generated by weight-one states.
result: They show that such algebras are finite tensor products of Virasoro minimal models or simple affine vertex operator algebras at positive integral levels, respectively, and consequently satisfy C2-cofiniteness and regularity.
conclusion: Zhu's conjecture holds for these two broad classes of rational vertex operator algebras, and all such algebras are regular.

title: Ramification Of Weighted Central Paths And Super-linear Interior-Point Methods For Semi-definite Optimization
authors: Ali Mohammad-Nezhad, Pouya Sampourmahani, Tamas Terlaky
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The local convergence of primal-dual interior-point methods for semi-definite optimization is closely tied to the regularity of the central path at its limiting point. Without strict complementarity, the central path can exhibit fractional power asymptotics and need not be differentiable in the ordinary barrier parameter. We show that this obstruction can be removed simultaneously for a family of weighted \AHO~central paths. More precisely, there exists a common ramification exponent [MATH] such that all weighted paths in a fixed neighborhood of the identity become analytic at the limiting point after the reparametrization [MATH]. Using higher-order derivatives of these reparametrized paths, we construct a feasible [MATH]th-order predictor-corrector interior-point method. Under a uniform predictor regularity condition, and without assuming strict complementarity, we prove that the normalized complementarity gaps converge with [MATH]-order at least [MATH], where [MATH] is the reparametrization exponent used by the method. We also establish super-linear convergence of the simultaneously vanishing primal-dual blocks, derive an explicit quantitative reduction bound throughout the predictor regularity region, and obtain a doubly logarithmic outer iteration bound once the iterates enter the local super-linear regime. Finally, we illustrate the predicted higher-order behavior on a collection of degenerate and non-degenerate semi-definite optimization problems.
tldr: The paper studies the local convergence of primal-dual interior-point methods for semi-definite optimization by analyzing the analyticity of weighted central paths under a common ramification exponent.
motivation: Without strict complementarity, the central path of semi-definite programs can have fractional-power asymptotics and fail to be differentiable in the barrier parameter, obstructing higher-order interior-point methods.
method: The authors prove that a family of weighted AHO central paths becomes analytic after a common reparametrization, then use higher-order derivatives of these reparametrized paths to build a feasible higher-order predictor-corrector interior-point method.
result: Under a uniform predictor regularity condition and without strict complementarity, normalized complementarity gaps converge with order at least equal to the reparametrization exponent, with super-linear convergence of simultaneously vanishing primal-dual blocks and a doubly logarithmic outer iteration bound.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous convergence theory for super-linear higher-order interior-point methods on degenerate semi-definite programs, illustrated numerically on degenerate and non-degenerate instances.

title: Measures Of Maximal Entropy For Monotone Factors Of Smooth Surface Diffeomorphisms
authors: Sylvain Crovisier, Alejo Garc\'ia-Sassi, Yuri Lima, F\'abio Tal
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by Garc\'ia-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.
tldr: The paper proves uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy for transitive monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms with positive topological entropy.
motivation: Monotone factors are natural quotients of surface dynamics, and understanding their measure-theoretic entropy structure connects topological entropy to invariant measures.
method: The authors analyze homoclinic classes and ergodic measures of positive entropy, showing that the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on the relevant class and that other classes map to periodic orbits.
result: They establish existence and uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy for such factors, with entropy equal to that of a single homoclinic class, and apply this to the essential factor of pseudo-Anosov-isotopic diffeomorphisms.
conclusion: The essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and fully supported, extending structural results for surface diffeomorphism factors.

title: Continuous-time q-Learning For Finite-Horizon Portfolio Choice With Optimal Stopping In Jump-Diffusion Markets
authors: Can Yang Tingting Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a structured continuous-time q-learning framework for finite-horizon investment and optimal stopping under jump-diffusion dynamics with unknown parameters. A penalty approximation transforms the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman variational inequality into an HJB equation with a binary control for the stopping penalty. An auxiliary state incorporates the resulting control-dependent discount factor into a Markovian formulation. We randomize controls on the mixed action space and introduce Shannon entropy regularization, establishing policy improvement and martingale characterizations of the continuous-time q-function. These results motivate a structured q-learning algorithm that constructs the q-function from the penalty HJB equation and jointly learns the value function and unknown generator parameters from sample paths. We apply the method to portfolio choice with optimal stopping in a simulation study. We further conduct a two-asset empirical study, evaluating learned strategies on bootstrap paths from held-out test returns versus an MLE-finite difference benchmark.
tldr: The paper develops a continuous-time q-learning framework for finite-horizon portfolio choice with optimal stopping under jump-diffusion market dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to solve investment and optimal stopping problems when jump-diffusion parameters are unknown, using a reinforcement-learning approach rather than relying on fully specified models.
method: They transform an HJB variational inequality via penalty approximation, randomize controls on a mixed action space with Shannon entropy regularization, and construct a structured q-learning algorithm that jointly learns the q-function, value function, and generator parameters from sample paths.
result: The method is tested in simulation and in a two-asset empirical study, where learned strategies are evaluated on bootstrap paths against an MLE-finite-difference benchmark.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured continuous-time reinforcement-learning approach for portfolio choice with optimal stopping in jump-diffusion markets, but it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Hybrid Newton-BFGS High-index Saddle Dynamics For Accelerating Saddle-point Searches
authors: Jianyuan Yin, Lei Zhang, Shixue Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) method for accelerating saddle-point searches. The method constructs a Newton correction on the unstable subspace from the available negative eigenpairs, while BFGS updates based on projected secant information approximate the inverse Hessian on the stable subspace. By combining Newton and quasi-Newton corrections, the method incorporates curvature information in both subspaces while preserving the ascent-descent structure of HiSD. Accounting for the evolving stable subspaces, we establish local [MATH]-superlinear convergence of the full-memory version near nondegenerate saddle points under suitable assumptions. We further develop a limited-memory version for large-scale problems and provide fixed-step and line search strategies. Numerical experiments show local convergence behavior consistent with the theory and demonstrate acceleration on ill-conditioned problems and degenerate saddle manifolds in neural-network loss landscapes. The method also supports efficient upward and downward saddle searches for a liquid crystal model, further illustrating its broad applicability to saddle-point computation.
tldr: The paper introduces a hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) algorithm that combines Newton corrections on the unstable subspace with limited-memory BFGS updates on the evolving stable subspace to accelerate saddle-point searches.
motivation: Existing HiSD methods converge slowly on ill-conditioned problems and degenerate saddle manifolds because they lack curvature information, so a faster method is needed for large-scale saddle-point computation.
method: The authors build a Newton correction from available negative eigenpairs on the unstable subspace, while BFGS updates based on projected secant information approximate the inverse Hessian on the stable subspace. They prove local superlinear convergence for the full-memory version near nondegenerate saddle points and develop a limited-memory version with fixed-step and line-search strategies.
result: Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical local convergence and show acceleration on ill-conditioned problems and degenerate saddle manifolds in neural-network loss landscapes, and the method also enables efficient upward and downward saddle searches for a liquid crystal model.
conclusion: Hybridizing Newton and quasi-Newton corrections yields a practical and theoretically grounded acceleration of HiSD for large-scale saddle-point searches.

title: Beyond Proof Of Possession: A Relational Theory Of Authority
authors: Nicola Gallo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-of-Possession (PoP) establishes that an executor controls an artifact (key, token, credential, or capability), but such control alone determines neither the executor's relational profile nor the causal history of an execution occurrence. We separate PoP from Proof of Relationship (PoR), the semantic property that one execution occurrence validly continues another, and from authorization, which is occurrence-sensitive. The foundational change is in the semantic domain of authorization: from holders and authority-bearing artifacts to execution occurrences situated in causal histories. We give authorization models an observation-based occurrence verdict and a separate transition-admissibility relation; kernel inclusion yields a partial order on observation-kernel classes. Building on Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) and Proof-of-Continuity (PoC), we classify executors by authorization-relevant equivalence relations whose quotients form relational profile spaces, with positive predicates over profile transitions forming a distributive lattice. This adds relational attenuation to authority attenuation: along a valid causal history, [MATH] and [MATH]. We prove dual monotonicity, combined closure, and origin relational closure. Two occurrences of the same authenticated executor, with the same profile and possession evidence, need not be authorization-equivalent, and within a valid PIC lineage a deputy's independent authority cannot be imported outside the origin context. Finally, we prove that the executor-dependent decision factors through the relational profile and is invariant under sound mechanisms establishing it: successor-side PoP is a possible evidence mechanism, not a necessary premise of authorization. Under explicit Witness Assumptions, a boundary-witnessed checkpoint construction realizes the premises without successor-side PoP.
tldr: The paper proposes a relational theory of authorization that replaces holder-based proofs of possession with occurrence-based, causally situated authorization verdicts grounded in provenance identity continuity.
motivation: Proof-of-Possession only shows an executor controls an artifact, which says nothing about whether a given execution validly continues another or about the executor's relational profile and causal history, so authorization semantics need a richer foundation.
method: The authors separate PoP from Proof of Relationship and authorization, define observation-based occurrence verdicts plus a transition-admissibility relation, build a partial order on observation-kernel classes, and classify executors via authorization-relevant equivalence relations whose quotients yield relational profile spaces with distributive lattices of positive predicates.
result: They prove dual monotonicity, combined closure, and origin relational closure, show that two occurrences of the same authenticated executor with identical profile and possession evidence need not be authorization-equivalent, and prove the executor-dependent decision factors through the relational profile and is invariant under sound mechanisms, with successor-side PoP as merely possible evidence.
conclusion: Authorization is fundamentally relational and occurrence-sensitive rather than artifact-centric; a boundary-witnessed checkpoint construction can realize the needed premises under explicit witness assumptions without requiring successor-side PoP.

title: JailBound: FOL-Guided Jailbreak Evaluation For Exploring Llm Behavioral Boundaries
authors: Fazong Wu, Xin Wang, Ming Yang, Zhenyong Zhang, Xiaoming Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as general-purpose conversational assistants, they must handle diverse user requests while reliably refusing harmful ones. Jailbreak attacks craft adversarial instructions or conversational contexts to elicit unsafe responses despite these safeguards. However, existing jailbreak benchmarks often rely on manually designed or collected prompts, making it difficult to systematically extend coverage to new threat conditions. Moreover, existing attack search methods typically optimize for attack success rate (ASR), providing limited insight into how model behavior changes locally between safe refusal and unsafe response. To address these limitations, we present JailBound, a unified jailbreak evaluation framework that combines automated benchmark construction with first-order loss (FOL)-guided dual-branch search. JailBound organizes threats by risk category, application domain, and attack type. Conditioned on this taxonomy, a fine-tuned meta-attack generator synthesizes evaluation prompts across diverse threat conditions. FOL serves as a local sensitivity signal for exploring high-value attack states and behavior-sensitive states. We evaluate JailBound across 46 LLMs from 13 model families under a unified experimental protocol. Under matched settings, the High-Value Branch improves average ASR over a ZOL-only baseline by 5.1 and 4.9 percentage points across the two evaluation settings. Under local perturbations, states from the Safety-Sensitivity Branch exhibit higher behavioral flip rates than those from the High-Value Branch across all tested radii for JailBound and S-Eval, indicating greater local sensitivity of judge-assigned safety labels. Warning: this paper includes examples that may be offensive or harmful.
tldr: JailBound is an automated jailbreak-evaluation framework for LLMs that combines a taxonomy-conditioned meta-attack generator with a first-order-loss-guided dual-branch search to map model behavioral boundaries between safe refusal and unsafe response.
motivation: Existing jailbreak benchmarks rely on manually designed or collected prompts, limiting systematic coverage of new threat conditions, and standard attack-search methods optimize only for attack success rate without revealing local behavior changes near the safety boundary.
method: The authors organize threats by risk category, application domain, and attack type, then use a fine-tuned meta-attack generator to synthesize prompts across these conditions; first-order loss is used as a local sensitivity signal to drive a dual-branch (high-value and safety-sensitivity) search over attack states.
result: Across 46 LLMs from 13 model families under a unified protocol, the High-Value Branch improves average ASR by 5.1 and 4.9 percentage points over a ZOL-only baseline in two evaluation settings, and Safety-Sensitivity states show higher behavioral flip rates under local perturbations.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic, extensible way to build jailbreak benchmarks and to probe local behavioral sensitivity of safety labels, offering finer-grained insight than ASR-only optimization.

title: Selecting The Best Uav Pursuer For Minimum Time Moving Target Interception Among Obstacles
authors: Masuda Akter M. M. Rizvi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A team of unmanned aerial vehicles (pursuers) with different positions, headings, speeds, minimum turning radii and launch delays must respond to a target that moves at constant velocity through a region containing static circular obstacles. Only one pursuer is launched, namely the one that can intercept the target first. We present a computationally efficient, obstacle-aware interceptor-selection framework for this setting. The interception problem of each pursuer is posed as a minimum-time optimal control problem and is solved over an explicit family of candidate path types through an arc-parameterised nonlinear programme in which the obstacles are toured tangentially and every part of the path is kept out of every obstacle by exact (not sampled) distance constraints. A closed-form lower bound, obtained by relaxing the curvature and obstacle constraints, is combined with the verified feasible interception times in a bound-and-select algorithm. We prove that the pruning is certified: a pursuer is skipped only if it cannot improve the best verified interception time, so bound-and-select returns the same pursuer and the same time as solving every pursuer, and the method reports a boundary on the optimal team interception time. Numerical experiments with solver diagnostics and repeated random starts, sensitivity studies in the target speed (with the selection crossover located by bisection), the launch delay, the turning radius and the obstacle configuration, a comparison with nearest-pursuer, fastest-pursuer and straight-line-time selection rules on random scenarios, a computational comparison with full enumeration for growing team sizes, and a geographic case study show that the selected pursuer is frequently neither the nearest nor the fastest, and that lower-bound pruning removes a large part of the computational effort without changing the decision.
tldr: The paper presents a certified bound-and-select algorithm for choosing which UAV pursuer can intercept a constant-velocity moving target soonest in an obstacle-cluttered environment.
motivation: Multi-UAV teams with heterogeneous kinematics and launch delays need a principled, computationally cheap way to decide which single pursuer to launch for minimum-time interception, rather than relying on heuristics such as nearest or fastest pursuer.
method: Each pursuer's interception is cast as a minimum-time optimal control problem solved over an arc-parameterised family of candidate paths with exact obstacle-distance constraints; a closed-form curvature- and obstacle-relaxed lower bound is combined with verified feasible times in a pruning algorithm.
result: Numerical experiments, sensitivity studies, and a geographic case study show the selected pursuer is often neither the nearest nor the fastest, while lower-bound pruning substantially reduces computation without altering the certified decision.
conclusion: Bound-and-select yields the same pursuer and interception time as exhaustive enumeration while providing a certified boundary on the optimal team interception time, making it practical for real-time pursuer selection.

title: Online Optimization For Controlling Hvac Systems
authors: Tong Wu, Dominik Baumann, Angela Fontan, Nicola Bastianello
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems account for a significant portion of buildings' energy consumption, motivating the design of energy- and cost-efficient control strategies. However, conventional strategies employ simple, reactive control, without incorporating a model. Therefore, in this paper we adopt an economic model predictive control framework and focus on designing online algorithms to solve the control input design problems with a limited computational budget. In particular, we propose two tailored online algorithms based on projected gradient descent, with a custom projection routine, and the projected primal-dual method. We discuss the pros and cons of both algorithm designs, focusing in particular on computational efficiency. We further compare them through numerical experiments simulating the control of an HVAC system over the course of a day. The results show that computationally efficient online solvers for HVAC systems control are indeed possible. Moreover, the performance closely matches that of a baseline algorithm with unlimited computational budget, in terms of reference temperature tracking and comfort temperature range enforcement.
tldr: The paper develops computationally efficient online algorithms for economic model predictive control of HVAC systems.
motivation: HVAC systems consume a large share of building energy, but conventional reactive control lacks predictive modeling and can be inefficient.
method: It adopts an economic model predictive control framework and proposes two online algorithms based on projected gradient descent with a custom projection routine and a projected primal-dual method.
result: Numerical experiments show that the proposed efficient online solvers closely match a baseline with unlimited computational budget in temperature tracking and comfort enforcement.
conclusion: Computationally efficient online solvers for HVAC control are feasible, though the work is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained Llm Reasoning For Technique Identification From Malware Reports
authors: Hongyu She, Yiling He, Mengda Xie, Yiping Liu, Xingzhi Qian, Zhan Qin, Lorenzo Cavallaro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mapping behavioral intelligence in malware analysis reports to ATT&CK techniques supports threat analysis and defense, but reliable identification remains challenging. Supporting evidence is often scattered across long, heterogeneous reports, while closely related techniques share behavioral cues and differ only in subtle but decisive details. While large language models (LLMs) can use external knowledge to interpret reports, they may assign techniques based on plausible associations rather than sufficient evidence. We present MEvince, a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework for report-level malware technique identification. Its core is a shared behavioral representation connecting report observations to technique definitions. This representation is built through agentic mining of technique documentation and supports two online stages: 1) primitive-guided extraction uses behavioral primitives to structure LLM-extracted observations, link them to source passages, and group dispersed evidence; 2) evidence-aligned retrieval matches this evidence to technique profiles through the same concepts, retaining likely candidates and confusable alternatives for LLM comparison of distinguishing behaviors. Controls at both stages validate evidence references and check technique-specific requirements. The representation also supports adaptation without parameter updates, where offline agentic audits diagnose concept weaknesses and refine extraction or retrieval policies. We evaluate MEvince against 11 baselines spanning four method families using a dataset of 610 public malware reports referenced by MITRE ATT&CK. MEvince improves exact-ID F1 over the strongest baseline by 17.4%, and its concept-guided retrieval increases gold-label candidate coverage from 31.6% to 47.9%. With a small adaptation set, offline refinement yields further gains and outperforms baselines that update model parameters.
tldr: MEvince is a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework that maps observations in malware analysis reports to MITRE ATT&CK techniques via a shared behavioral representation.
motivation: Reliable ATT&CK technique identification from long, heterogeneous malware reports is hard because evidence is scattered and confusable techniques differ only in subtle behavioral details, while LLMs tend to rely on plausible associations rather than sufficient evidence.
method: The authors build a shared behavioral representation by agentically mining technique documentation, then use it in two online stages: primitive-guided extraction that structures observations and links them to source passages, and evidence-aligned retrieval that matches grouped evidence to technique profiles, with validation controls at both stages and offline agentic audits for adaptation without parameter updates.
result: Evaluated on 610 public MITRE ATT&CK-referenced malware reports against 11 baselines from four method families, MEvince improves exact-ID F1 by 17.4% over the strongest baseline and raises gold-label candidate coverage from 31.6% to 47.9%, with further gains from offline refinement.
conclusion: Knowledge-constrained, evidence-grounded LLM reasoning substantially improves report-level malware technique identification and can be adapted without retraining model parameters.

title: Drift-Resilient Predictive Interference Management: Online Adaptation Of An Extreme-Value Predictor
authors: Aamir Mahmood, Fateme Salehi, Nurul Huda Mahmood, Song Han
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predictive interference management supports ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) by allocating finite-blocklength resources against a high conditional quantile of next-slot interference. Building on an extreme-value-theory/kernel-density-estimation (EVT/KDE) predictor with quantile-defined interference states, this paper makes the predictor resilient to unannounced shifts in the interference distribution. Its cumulative refitting on all past observations does not specify how the state partition and retained samples should evolve after a regime change. We show that drift first makes the quantile partition inefficient: cumulative refitting preserves tail support and coverage but cannot recover conditional resolution, and pays for it in channel use, whereas discarding history starves the tail estimator. We therefore propose event-triggered quantile-space adaptation. A nonparametric cumulative sum (CUSUM) on the predictor's level stream detects change. At each confirmed event, the quantile partition is re-derived from post-change observations, retained history is re-binned under it, and each state is refit from a bounded per-state memory, capped to balance stale-regime bias against tail-estimation variance, with a closed-form L-moment tail estimator. At a nominal coverage target [MATH], relative to matched cumulative refitting with fixed states, the proposed method reduces channel use by [MATH]--[MATH] and quantile pinball loss by [MATH]--[MATH] across abrupt, incremental, compound, downward, and reversal drift, with coverage changing by [MATH] to [MATH] percentage points. At matched achieved coverage, it saves [MATH]--[MATH] of channel uses, while resource use in load-only and stationary cases changes by less than [MATH]. With [MATH] samples per state and [MATH] states, predictor memory is bounded at [MATH] rather than growing as [MATH].
tldr: This paper develops an event-triggered adaptive extreme-value predictor for interference management in URLLC wireless networks, making quantile-based prediction robust to distribution drift.
motivation: Predictive interference management for ultra-reliable low-latency communication requires reliable high-quantile interference estimates, but cumulative refitting of existing EVT/KDE predictors becomes inefficient after unannounced regime changes.
method: The authors use a nonparametric CUSUM on the predictor's level stream to detect drift, then re-derive the quantile partition from post-change observations, re-bin retained history, and refit each state from bounded per-state memory with a closed-form L-moment tail estimator.
result: Relative to cumulative refitting with fixed states, the method reduces channel use and quantile pinball loss across abrupt, incremental, compound, downward, and reversal drift while maintaining coverage close to target, and bounds predictor memory.
conclusion: Event-triggered quantile-space adaptation improves the resilience of predictive interference management under distribution drift with modest resource overhead in stationary and load-only cases.

title: The Promise Of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting
authors: Abhishek Satyam, Hossein Siadati, Haadi Jafarian, Sima Jafarikhah, Juntao Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.08170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scammers have increasingly adopted AI-driven capabilities, evolving from automated message generation to fully agentic conversational systems that scale operations and maximize the exploitation of fraudulent resources before detection and takedown. In parallel, agentic scambaiting has emerged as a defensive approach in which autonomous agents impersonate potential victims and engage scammers in sustained interactions to extract actionable threat intelligence, such as mule bank accounts and cryptocurrency wallet addresses, that can be reported to disrupt fraudulent infrastructures. Together, these developments transform online fraud into an adversarial socio-technical ecosystem in which autonomous scamming and scambaiting agents engage in deceptive interactions while competing over the discovery, preservation, and exploitation of one another's resources. A fundamental and largely unexplored question is how defensive scambaiting can remain effective in an agent-to-agent environment, and under what conditions either side gains a strategic advantage. In this paper, we present a formal model of agent-to-agent fraud interactions that captures the strategic decision spaces available to both attackers and defenders. Using this framework, we analyze the dynamics of engagement, resource consumption, belief adaptation, and disruption outcomes. We find that scammer profitability turns negative once baiting-agent prevalence exceeds certain thresholds, and that when both sides improve at the same pace, defender investment in mimicry quality outpaces equivalent gains in scammer detection capability, so the arms race favors the defender under our baseline parameters. Our model and findings provide insights into the stability, scalability, and long-term effectiveness of autonomous defensive agents in an evolving AI-mediated fraud landscape.
tldr: The paper formalizes agent-to-agent interactions between AI-driven scammers and autonomous scambaiting defenders, analyzing strategic engagement dynamics and disruption outcomes.
motivation: Scammers have moved to fully agentic conversational systems, prompting defensive agentic scambaiting; it is unclear whether such defense remains effective in an agent-versus-agent adversarial ecosystem.
method: The authors build a formal game-theoretic/strategic model of attacker and defender decision spaces, capturing engagement dynamics, resource consumption, belief adaptation, and disruption outcomes.
result: Scammer profitability turns negative above certain baiting-agent prevalence thresholds, and under baseline parameters defender investment in mimicry quality outpaces equivalent scammer detection gains, favoring the defender.
conclusion: The model offers insight into the stability, scalability, and long-term effectiveness of autonomous defensive agents in AI-mediated fraud landscapes.

title: Rest: Routing With En-route Seating Thresholds For Pedestrian Accessibility
authors: Himshikhar Mazumdar Nir Fulman
abstract: ArXiv:2611.07095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public seating can support walking by providing opportunities to rest at useful positions along complete journeys. We introduce a route-based framework that assesses nearby seating, access to everyday destinations, and whether rests are well spaced along routes. One method finds the shortest route that does not exceed a chosen distance without rest; another allows longer stretches but adds a cost expressed as equivalent walking distance. We apply the framework to Mannheim, Germany. With a 1,000 m travel budget and a 500 m limit on walking without an opportunity to rest, 99.5% of older residents in Feudenheim lived within 500 m of a rest, yet only 33.5% could reach at least one destination in each of five categories (food shops, pharmacies, primary healthcare, public transport, and community services) on ordinary shortest routes meeting this limit. Finding alternative routes with sufficiently spaced rests increased this share to 61.4%; allowing longer stretches with an added cost raised it to 76.2%, compared with 89.7% when resting needs were ignored. Across Mannheim, 20.2% of older residents lost access to a reachable category when routes required a resting opportunity every 500 m, versus 7.1% when longer stretches were allowed at extra cost. Compared with the shortest physical distance, the least burdensome routes incurred extra costs from seating gaps: a median of 7.3 m of equivalent walking distance across city areas (90th percentile: 45.9 m). Better-placed seating could reduce this burden without changing street layouts. These measures help planners identify deficiencies, test improvements and guide route choices.
tldr: This paper introduces a route-based framework for assessing public seating availability and spacing along pedestrian journeys, applied to Mannheim, Germany, to evaluate accessibility for older residents.
motivation: Public seating supports walking by offering rest opportunities along complete journeys, but existing accessibility measures typically ignore the placement and spacing of rests relative to routes and destinations.
